Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
PROMOTION OF DOMESTIC CONTAINER MANUFACTURING AND MARITIME SELF-RELIANCE
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi

An order for shipping containers was placed by a global shipping line on an Indian container manufacturer. The domestically produced prototype container was unveiled at Dadri, Uttar Pradesh on 03.07.2026. The shipping containers are produced in accordance with internationally accepted quality and safety standards, including International Organization for Standardization (ISO) specifications and the International Convention for Safe Containers (CSC).

The above global shipping line has reportedly placed an order for 1,000 shipping containers on an Indian container manufacturer. Procurement of Indian-manufactured containers by global shipping lines demonstrates international confidence in India’s manufacturing quality, engineering capability, and adherence to global safety standards. It also signals the emergence of India as a reliable partner in the global maritime logistics supply chain.

The Government in Budget Speech 2026-27 has announced a Scheme for container manufacturing in India with a budget outlay of Rs. 10,000 crore aimed at creating globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in the country.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
COASTAL CARGO PROMOTION SCHEME
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:39PM by PIB Delhi

In Union Budget 2026, it was announced to launch a Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme to increase the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping from 6% to 12% by 2047. At present, the proposed Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme is at formation stage.

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways has been actively pursuing the promotion of coastal shipping through various initiatives. In this regard, the Government has taken following measures:

40% concession on port charges (vessel and cargo-related charges) is provided for coastal cargo vessels.

Priority berthing policy for coastal vessels has been notified to reduce turnaround time for coastal vessels and improve their utilization.

GST on bunker fuel used by Indian-flag vessels has been reduced from 18% to 5%.

Green channel clearance introduced for faster evacuation of coastal cargo at ports.

The Coastal Shipping Act, 2025 enacted to promote coastal shipping.

The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways has sanctioned 30 infrastructure development projects for financial assistance under the Sagarmala scheme to promote Ro-Ro, Ro-Pax and Passenger ferry services. Out of these, 18 projects worth ₹ 739 crore have been completed.

On account of completed projects, for instance, Ro-Pax ferry on the Ghogha– Hazira route in the state of Gujarat cuts a 12-hour road journey down to 4-hour sea route and Ro-Pax ferry on Mumbai –Mandwa route in the state of Maharashtra reduces travel time to Alibaug from 4 hours by road to just 1 hour by sea route.

The Ro-Pax and Passenger ferry services have benefited more than 65 lakh passengers and more than 15 lakh vehicles and cargo carrying trucks.

40% concession on port charges (vessel and cargo-related charges) is provided for coastal cargo vessels.

Dedicated coastal berths have been developed at 10 major ports. The details are available at Annexure-I

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
NHAI Undertakes DPR Preparation to Decongest Sarai Kale Khan Loop on DND–Sohna National Highway Corridor
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:24PM by PIB Delhi

In order to improve traffic flow and enhance commuter convenience in the National Capital Region (NCR), NHAI has undertaken preparation of the Detailed Project Report (DPR) to address traffic congestion at the Sarai Kale Khan Loop, which is a critical junction of the DND–Sohna section on NH-148NA. The DPR will examine long-term traffic management and engineering solutions for one of the busiest transport nodes in Delhi and will complement the ongoing infrastructure development initiatives in the region.

The Sarai Kale Khan Loop serves as a strategic convergence point for traffic originating from Ashram, Noida and Sarai Kale Khan. With the upcoming commissioning of the DND–Sohna National Highway corridor, the location is expected to witness a substantial increase in traffic volumes, necessitating timely intervention to ensure smooth and efficient traffic movement.

Recognizing the strategic importance of the corridor, NHAI will undertake DPR preparation on priority to identify comprehensive engineering solutions to decongest the junction and improve traffic circulation. The DPR will evaluate suitable infrastructure interventions aimed at enhancing capacity, reducing travel time and ensuring safety as well as more efficient movement of vehicles through the corridor. It will also ensure that the operational benefits of the DND–Sohna corridor are fully realized upon its commissioning by enabling seamless connectivity at this critical interchange.

The initiative reflects NHAI's continued focus on improving urban connectivity, reducing congestion and delivering enhanced travel experience for road users.

 

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
The National SC-ST Hub Scheme is helping in reliable supply chains, increased employment generation and participation of SC/ST entrepreneurs in India's industrial ecosystem
NSSH is Empowering SC-ST Entrepreneurs: Enabling Technology, Capacity and Market Access for Inclusive Growth
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi

The National SC-ST Hub Scheme (NSSH) scheme, under the Ministry of MSME, continues to strengthen the competitiveness of SC-ST entrepreneurs by enabling technology upgradation, enhancing business capabilities and facilitating greater participation in public procurement. Through interventions such as the Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS) and the Business Acceleration Programme (BAP), the scheme is helping enterprises overcome operational constraints, adopt modern technologies, augment compliance and access larger institutional markets.

  1.  Engineering Excellence through Technology Upgradation: The Journey of Varun Enterprises, Punjab

Led by Mr. Hukum Chand, Varun Enterprises has established a strong presence in the engineering and manufacturing sector by delivering reliable, high-quality industrial solutions. With focus on precision, quality and compliance, the enterprise steadily built its capabilities to meet the requirements of institutional and Government buyers.

Overcoming Capacity Constraints

As the enterprise expands, adopting advanced technology became essential to enhance productivity, reduce turnaround time and remain competitive in an evolving market. Hence, with support from the National SC-ST Hub Office, Ludhiana, Varun Enterprises availed ₹15.67 lakh under the SCLCSS during 2021-22. This support enabled the installation of advanced manufacturing equipment, including a fibre laser cutting system, CNC hydraulic press brake, air compressor, UPS systems and supporting electrical infrastructure. The upgraded machines significantly enhanced production efficiency, precision, quality and operational reliability, enabling the enterprise to participate in larger procurement. 

A significant milestone was securing a ₹95.99 lakh purchase order from the Modern Coach Factory (MCF), Rae Bareli, for supply of connection boxes in rail coaches. This achievement reinforced the enterprise's credibility as a reliable supplier capable of delivering quality engineering solutions for the railways.

Positioning for Long-Term Growth

With modern manufacturing capabilities, Varun Enterprises has positioned its footprint in high-value engineering products. The support received under SCLCSS has enabled the enterprise to pursue new opportunities in Government and institutional markets while laying a strong foundation for sustained growth.

 

  1.   Scaling Excellence in Petroleum Logistics through Strategic Capability Enhancement: The Journey of Raju Thangavelu, Tamilnadu

Based in Tiruvallur, Mr. Raju Thangavelu has built a dependable enterprise in the petroleum logistics sector, specializing in the transportation of bulk fuels. By consistently adhering to stringent safety compliance and operational standards, the enterprise has established itself as a trusted service provider with a growing presence in Government procurement.

Overcoming Growth and Compliance Challenges

As demand for its services increased, the enterprise faced the challenge of expanding fleet capacity while meeting the stringent safety and regulatory requirements of oil marketing companies. To address these challenges, the enterprise availed ₹25 lakh under SCLCSS. The assistance upgraded transportation infrastructure and safety-compliant systems, strengthening fleet capacity, improving operational efficiency and enhancing service reliability, thereby, enabling the enterprise to meet evolving industry standards while improving its competitiveness.

Expanding Presence in Public Procurement.

The SCLCS support enabled the enterprise to secure large assignments in the public procurement ecosystem. A key milestone was the award of a transportation contract from Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) in April 2026, reflecting the enterprise's growing credibility and ability to execute large-scale transportation assignments in logistic sector.

  1. Transforming Healthcare Manufacturing through Integrated Business Support: The Journey of BOI (B. Ortho International Pvt. Ltd.), Jharkhand

Led by Mr. Rahul & Mrs. Divya from Ranchi, BOI (B. Ortho International Pvt. Ltd.) has established itself in the medical and orthopedic manufacturing sector by delivering quality products that meet stringent healthcare standards. With a strong focus on precision, compliance and reliability, the enterprise has steadily built its reputation in institutional and public sector markets.

Unlocking the Next Stage of Growth

As demand for their products increased, the need to upgrade machinery, improve operational efficiency and business capabilities became essential. Hence, with support from the National SC-ST Hub, Ranchi, the enterprise received assistance from both SCLCS and the Business Acceleration Programme (BAP). The SCLCS supported in installation of advanced machinery and production infrastructure, while BAP provided strategic mentorship, business guidance and market linkages. BOI significantly enhanced its production capacity and now manufactures approximately 50,000 pairs of latex surgical gloves per day. Improved manufacturing efficiency and quality standards helped double the enterprise's turnover from ₹15 lakh to ₹30 lakh, while its operations also generated local employment with around 60% women workforce participation, contributing to the regional economy.

 

A Common Story of Inclusive Enterprise Development

The success stories of Varun Enterprises (Punjab), Raju Thangavelu (Tamil Nadu), and BOI (B Ortho International Pvt. Ltd., Jharkhand) demonstrate how targeted support can transform enterprises into resilient and competitive businesses. By enhancing their capabilities, operational efficiency and participating in the public procurement process, it has enabled the SC-ST enterprises to contribute to the nation's inclusive economic growth.

These examples illustrate how the National SC-ST Hub Scheme is fostering inclusive entrepreneurship. The scheme is helping in reliable supply chains, increased employment generation and participation of SC/ST entrepreneurs in India's industrial ecosystem.

Moving Forward

As India continues to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities, the National SC-ST Hub scheme remains committed to empowering SC/ST entrepreneurs through technology upgradation, capacity building, business acceleration and market linkages. The success stories of Varun Enterprises, Raju Thangavelu, and BOI stand as an examples of how integrated policy support can transform entrepreneurial potential into long-term business success, contributing to the vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat.

For more details of the scheme, visit https://www.scsthub.in/

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Railways
item.description: Ministry of Railways India's First Direct Commercial Container Freight Train Reaches Nepal, Opening a New Chapter in Cross-border Trade and Connectivity 40-Wagon Freight Train from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar Operates Under Revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol Direct Rail Freight Service Reduces Transit Time, Logistics Costs and Cargo Handling, Strengthening India-Nepal Trade Ties Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:16PM by PIB Delhi Indian Railways has achieved a major milestone in strengthening India-Nepal freight connectivity with the successful operation of the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Railways
India's First Direct Commercial Container Freight Train Reaches Nepal, Opening a New Chapter in Cross-border Trade and Connectivity
40-Wagon Freight Train from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar Operates Under Revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol
Direct Rail Freight Service Reduces Transit Time, Logistics Costs and Cargo Handling, Strengthening India-Nepal Trade Ties
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:16PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has achieved a major milestone in strengthening India-Nepal freight connectivity with the successful operation of the first-ever direct commercial container freight train from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar Customs Yard, Nepal. The train, comprising 40 wagons carrying a consignment of canola, completed its journey under the revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol, marking a new chapter in rail-based cross-border freight movement.

The successful operation enables direct rail movement of containerised cargo from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar without transshipment at the border. The new arrangement is expected to substantially reduce transit time, logistics costs and cargo handling while improving the efficiency, reliability and competitiveness of cross-border trade between the two neighbouring countries. The milestone has been made possible through the implementation of the revised India-Nepal Rail Transit Protocol, which facilitates seamless end-to-end rail transportation of freight between the two countries.

The achievement builds upon the broad-gauge rail link between Jogbani (India) and Biratnagar (Nepal), inaugurated in June 2023 by the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India Shri Narendra Modi and the then Prime Minister of Nepal. Following the signing of the revised Letter of Exchange (LoE) in November 2025, direct commercial rail movement to Biratnagar has now become operational, opening new opportunities for bilateral trade and economic cooperation.

The direct freight service is expected to provide a significant boost to the movement of import and export cargo by offering a faster, more economical and environmentally sustainable mode of transportation. By reducing multiple handling points and improving supply chain efficiency, the initiative will benefit exporters, importers, logistics operators and industries engaged in cross-border trade.

The milestone also reflects Indian Railways' continued focus on expanding international rail connectivity, strengthening freight logistics and supporting the Government's vision of improving ease of doing business through modern transport infrastructure. Increased rail-based freight movement will contribute to lower logistics costs, improved cargo reliability and greener transportation while fostering stronger economic partnerships with neighbouring countries.

The successful operation of the first direct commercial container freight train to Nepal marks another important achievement in Indian Railways' efforts to build an integrated, efficient and future-ready freight network that supports regional trade, economic growth and seamless international connectivity.

 *****

Mahesh Kumar/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India's Toy Exports Soar 89.1%, Reflecting Strong Growth in Domestic Manufacturing
Toy Biz International 2026 Showcases 400 Indian Brands, Boosting Domestic Sales and Export Opportunities
Government Initiatives Boost Quality, Safety and Competitiveness of India's Toy Industry
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi

The 17th Toy Biz International B2B Exhibition was organized by the Toy Association of India from 4th to 7th July, 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Exhibition aimed at promoting Indian toys, facilitating business networking, and creating opportunities for growth in domestic sales and exports. It witnessed participation of 400 Indian toy brands, 100 international buyers from 40 countries, and around 30,000 business visitors. The exhibition provided platform for connecting manufacturers with wholesalers, retailers, distributors, institutional buyers and e-commerce platforms.

At present, there is no dedicated toy policy of the Government of India.

In 2018-19, Toys worth USD 371.7 Mn were imported into India. A large proportion of these toys were unsafe, substandard, counterfeit, and cheap. Further, a Mystery Shopping exercise conducted in 2019 revealed that only 33% toys in the domestic market were of acceptable quality as per BIS standards.

In order to improve the quality and safety of toys in the country and to promote the overall development of the Indian toy industry, the Government of India has undertaken several initiatives. The key initiatives are as follows:

  • Formulation of a comprehensive National Action Plan for Toys (NAPT), comprising 21 action points and coordinated by 14 Ministries and Departments. It focuses on promoting the design and development of toys based on Indian values, culture, and history; encouraging the use of toys as learning resources; organizing hackathons, toy fairs, and grand challenges for toy design and manufacturing; strengthening quality monitoring and restricting the import of substandard and unsafe toys; promoting indigenous toy clusters; and boosting domestic manufacturing.
  • Basic Custom Duty (BCD) on Toys (HS Code-9503) was increased from 20% to 60% in February 2020, and subsequently increased to 70% in 2023. Further, the BCD on Parts of Electronic Toys (HS 95030091) revised as 20% in the Budget F.Y. 2025-26.
  • A Quality Control Order (QCO) for Toys was issued on 25.02.2020, implemented with effect from 01.01.2021.
  • BIS has granted more than 1800 licenses to domestic manufacturers of toys and more than 50 licenses to foreign manufacturers for use of BIS Standard Mark on toys conforming to the Indian Standards for safety of toys.
  • The National Education Policy 2020 formulated by Ministry of Education focuses on play and activity-based learning. A handbook on ‘Toy Based Pedagogy’ has been published by NCERT with the objective of ensuring that the learning process for children is enjoyable and fun. It prescribes toys, especially based on indigenous toys and games to be used at different stages to help develop many competencies in young children.
  • Cluster-based approach adopted to support domestic Toy industry. The Ministry of MSMEs has approved 18 Toy clusters under the Scheme of Funds for the Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI), and the Ministry of Textiles is providing designing and tooling support to 40 Toy clusters.
  • More than 700 startups have been recognised by DPIIT under Startup India initiative.
  • More than 2,200 exporters have been supported under Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) scheme for exports of Toys.
  • Zero duty market access under India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), the India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement, and India-European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement, India-Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, and India-United Kingdom Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement.
  • Several promotional initiatives have also been undertaken to promote indigenous toys and encourage innovation, including Toycathon, Toy fairs, etc.

These initiatives have resulted in remarkable growth of the Indian Toy industry. As per a BIS survey conducted in 2025, 95% of toy samples were found conforming to the prescribed quality standards, as against 33% in 2019, indicating a substantial improvement in the quality of toys available in the Indian market.

Further, the Indian toy industry has emerged as a net exporter of toys with exports to countries including United States, United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Germany. The import of toys into India has declined by 37.5%, while toy exports have increased by 89.1%.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India's Exports Scale Record US$ 863.1 Billion in FY 2025–26, Driven by Strong Trade with UAE, UK and Australia
India's FTAs Deepen Global Market Access, Boost Export Diversification and Labour-Intensive Sectors
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi

India recorded highest-ever exports in FY 2025-26 reaching a record US$ 863.1 billion, with merchandise exports reaching US$ 441.8 billion and services exports expanding further to US$ 421.3 billion, reflecting the combined strength of India’s merchandise and services sectors in driving export growth. Destination-wise data is available for merchandise exports and FTA wise India’s merchandise exports during FY 2025-26 is given below in Table 1.

The Government monitors utilisation of preferential tariff benefits under newly operationalised trade agreements (signed post 2021) through Certificates of Origin and partner-country trade data.

  • India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA): Since its entry into force on 1st May 2022, 4.45 lakh Certificates of Origin have been issued, reflecting robust utilisation of tariff concessions by Indian exporters. Further, the number of tariff lines at the HS 8-digit level exported to the UAE increased from 7,546 in FY 2021-22 (pre-CEPA) to 8,053 in FY 2025-26, with exports across these tariff lines valued at US$ 37.3 billion. This represents an increase of 507 tariff lines (6.7%), indicating greater export diversification and deeper market penetration in the UAE market following the implementation of CEPA.
  • India-Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement (ECTA): Since its entry into force in December 2022, 2.73 lakh Certificates of Origin have been issued. Prior to ECTA, only 1,482 Certificate of Origin were issued in FY 2020-21. Following implementation of the Agreement, Certificate of Origin issuance increased significantly, with an average of approximately 45,527 Certificate of Origin issued annually. In FY 2021-22, 5396 tariff lines at HS 8 level and after FTA in FY 2025-26, 5668 tariff lines at HS 8 level valuing US$ 7.2 Bn. This represents an increase of 272 tariff lines, indicating greater export diversification and expanded market access following the implementation of ECTA.
  • India-Mauritius Comprehensive Economic Cooperation and Partnership Agreement (CECPA): The CECPA entered into force on 1 April 2021. The Agreement provides preferential market access for 310 Indian product lines in Mauritius and covers goods, services, Rules of Origin, customs procedures and economic cooperation. Indian exporters have availed preferential tariff benefits through the issuance of 1,956 Certificates of Origin under the Agreement. Further, the number of tariff lines at the HS 8-digit level exported to Mauritius increased from 3,593 in FY 2021-22 (pre-CECPA) to 4,345 in FY 2025-26, with exports across these tariff lines valued at approximately US$ 473 million. This represents an increase of 752 tariff lines (20.9%), indicating greater export diversification and expanded market access following the implementation of CECPA.
  • India–Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA): CEPA grants duty-free access to 99.38% of India’s exports to Oman by value, covering 98.08% of Oman’s tariff lines, making it one of India’s most comprehensive market access outcomes in the Gulf region. Since its entry into force on 1 June 2026, 783 Certificates of Origin have been issued. Further, the  number of tariff lines at the HS 8-digit level exported to Oman increased from 2,879 in May 2026 to 3,371 in June 2026. Exports across these tariff lines stood at US$ 622.8 million in June 2026, compared to US$ 402.7 million in May 2026 (month-on-month growth of 54.7%) and US$ 215.1 million in June 2025 (year-on-year growth of 189.6%), indicating enhanced market access and export diversification following the implementation of the Agreement.
  • India EFTA-TEPA: Under TEPA, EFTA has offered 92.2% of tariff lines encompassing 99.6% of India’s exports. Includes 100% of non-agricultural products and tariff concessions on Processed Agricultural Products (PAP). Since its entry into force in October 2025, 7885 Certificates of Origin have been issued reflecting impressive utilisation of tariff concessions by Indian exporters

The labour-intensive sectors have remained a key priority in India's recent FTA negotiations. Agreements concluded with the UAE, Australia, the United Kingdom, Oman, New Zealand and EFTA have secured improved market access while adopting a calibrated approach to safeguard sensitive domestic sectors. Collectively, these agreements provide preferential access to a substantial share of partner-country tariff lines, for instance, 99% of Indian exports to the UK, 97% of EU tariff lines covering about 99.5% of bilateral trade value, 100% duty-free access for Indian exports to New Zealand, 98% of Oman's tariff lines, and 99.6% of tariff lines under the India–EFTA TEPA. These agreements provide significant export opportunities for labour-intensive sectors such as textiles & apparel, leather & footwear, gems & jewellery, marine products, carpets, handicrafts and agricultural products, while preserving adequate policy space for sensitive domestic sectors through calibrated tariff liberalisation and transition arrangements. This balanced approach seeks to promote employment-intensive exports, strengthen domestic manufacturing competitiveness and deepen India's integration into global value chains.

The Government has established a comprehensive framework to monitor export performance across sectors, including labor-intensive segments, through a whole-of-Government approach involving all stakeholders - the Department of Commerce, Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Export Promotion Councils (EPCs), Commodity Boards, line Ministries, State Governments including districts and Indian Missions abroad.

The Department of Commerce has also significantly strengthened trade facilitation and trade intelligence platforms such as Trade e-Connect and the Trade Intelligence and Analytics (TIA) Portal. Trade e-Connect serves as a comprehensive exporter facilitation platform, integrating market intelligence, tariff information, non-tariff barriers, Rules of Origin guidance, buyer-seller information, trade events, country and product guides, and FTA-related advisory services to help exporters identify opportunities and effectively utilise preferential market access under India's FTAs. The platform also facilitates engagement between exporters, Indian Missions abroad and relevant government agencies, thereby reducing information asymmetries and improving access to international markets. The TIA Portal complements these efforts by providing extensive trade analytics, commodity-level data, partner-country information and interactive dashboards to support data-driven policymaking and real-time monitoring of export performance.

This information was given by Minister of State for Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Jitin Prasada in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

 

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Garima Singh/ Ishita Biswas

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :
Department of Fertilizers
Government Strengthens Measures to Ensure Timely Fertilizer Availability and Curb Black Marketing
Over 4.84 Lakh Raids Conducted in 2025 Against Black Marketing, Hoarding and Diversion of Fertilizers
Affordable Fertilizers Ensured Through Urea Subsidy, NBS Scheme and Continuous Supply Monitoring
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has reiterated its commitment to ensuring the timely and adequate availability of fertilizers to farmers while taking stringent action against black marketing, hoarding, diversion and sale of sub-standard fertilizers. A comprehensive mechanism has been put in place to ensure uninterrupted fertilizer supplies, maintain affordability and strengthen enforcement across the country.

To ensure seamless availability of fertilizers during every cropping season, the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with State Governments, assesses the State-wise and month-wise fertilizer requirement before each season. Based on these projections, the Department of Fertilizers allocates adequate quantities through monthly supply plans and continuously monitors availability. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is tracked through the Integrated Fertilizer Management System (iFMS). The Government also finalizes fertilizer imports well in advance to bridge the gap between domestic production and demand, coordinates with manufacturers and importers for timely supplies, works closely with the Ministry of Railways for priority movement of fertilizer rakes, and State Governments oversee district-level distribution. As a result, adequate availability of Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS was maintained across all States and Union Territories during FY 2025-26. State-wise details are provided in the below.

The Government continues to ensure that fertilizers remain affordable for farmers through the Urea Subsidy Scheme and the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme. Under the Urea Subsidy Scheme, the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) of a 45 kg bag of urea remains ₹242 per bag (exclusive of neem coating charges and applicable taxes), with the difference between the delivered cost and market realization reimbursed to manufacturers/importers as subsidy. Under the NBS Scheme, implemented since 1 April 2010, subsidy is provided on notified Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) fertilizers based on nutrient content and Point of Sale (PoS) sales. To keep DAP affordable at ₹1,350 per 50 kg bag during Kharif 2026, the Government has extended additional support of ₹3,500 per metric tonne over and above the NBS subsidy to imported and domestic DAP and imported TSP. This support covers transportation costs, international price fluctuations, GST component included in the MRP and a reasonable return of 4% of net MRP (excluding GST).

To further strengthen the P&K fertilizer sector, the Government has issued guidelines dated 18 January 2024 on the reasonableness of MRP, providing reasonable profit margins of 8% for importers, 10% for manufacturers and 12% for integrated manufacturers. New manufacturing units and expansion of existing capacities have been recognized under the NBS Scheme, while the number of fertilizer grades covered under the scheme has increased from 22 in 2021 to 28. Freight subsidy on Single Super Phosphate (SSP) has also been continued since Kharif 2022 to promote the use of indigenously manufactured phosphatic fertilizers. Nutrient subsidy rates are reviewed on a biannual basis to ensure continued availability of fertilizers.

The Government is also closely monitoring enforcement actions against black marketing, hoarding, diversion and sale of sub-standard fertilizers. According to information received from DA&FW, 4,84,663 raids were conducted across the country during 2025, leading to the issuance of 17,392 show-cause notices, suspension or cancellation of 6,941 licences, and registration of 847 FIRs against defaulters. DA&FW regularly follows up with State Governments to ensure strict enforcement and prevent malpractices. Fertilizer requirements are assessed through Zonal Conferences for Agricultural Inputs, where States and Union Territories project their seasonal demand based on gross cropped area, irrigated area, fertilizer consumption patterns and crop-wise nutrient recommendations linked to soil health.

The Government has also taken several measures to ensure the availability of safe and quality pesticides. The Registration Committee constituted under the Insecticides Act, 1968 registers pesticides only after evaluating their efficacy and safety. The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare periodically reviews registered pesticides based on scientific evidence, reports from State Governments and international developments relating to toxicity or environmental concerns. Registered pesticides, when used in accordance with prescribed label claims and leaflets, do not pose harm to human beings, animals or the environment.

To monitor pesticide residues, the Government has been implementing the Monitoring of Pesticide Residues at National Level (MPRNL) project since 2005-06. Under the project, 40 NABL-accredited laboratories analyse samples of vegetables, fruits, spices, cereals, pulses, herbs, fish and marine products, meat, eggs, tea, milk and water collected from across the country. Monthly reports on pesticide residues, including samples exceeding the Maximum Residue Limits (MRLs) prescribed by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) and cases of off-label pesticide use, are shared with State Agricultural Departments to promote safe and judicious pesticide use and encourage Integrated Pest Management (IPM) practices.

The Ministry also implements the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and the Insecticides Rules, 1971 to ensure the availability of quality pesticides. Insecticide Inspectors appointed by the Central and State Governments regularly collect samples from manufacturing units and retail outlets for quality testing. Samples are analyzed by notified Insecticide Analysts, and prosecution is initiated against manufacturers or dealers where samples fail to meet prescribed quality standards. To improve affordability and availability, the Registration Committee grants registrations for generic pesticides expeditiously, with the registration fee under Section 9(4) fixed at ₹25,000, compared to ₹2,25,000 under Section 9(3) of the Act.

This information was provided by Smt. Anupriya Patel, Minister of State in the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha today.

***

Neeraj Kumar Bhatt/Shatrughna Prasad

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
INLAND FISHERIES INFRASTRUCTURE UNDER PMMSY
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:09PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India has been implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total cost of Rs. 20,750 crore with effect from the financial year 2020-21 for the development of fisheries sector in all States/Union Territories including Uttar Pradesh.  The State-wise details of projects approved under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for overall development of fisheries including infrastructure, including ponds, reservoirs, hatcheries, feed mills and cold chain facilities from 2020-21 till date are furnished at Annexure-I.

Further, the Department under the PMMSY has accorded approval to the various fisheries developmental proposals of Government of Uttar Pradesh at a total cost of Rs.  1294.32 crore with central liability of Rs. 412.30 crore. Against this central liability,  Rs.336.61 crore has been released for development of Fisheries in the State against which  an expenditure of Rs. 316.61 Crore has been incurred.  As reported by the Government of Uttar Pradesh, PMMSY has been implemented across all districts including the eastern region of the State and assistance is provided for scientific aquaculture, integrated fish farming, pond development, hatcheries, reservoirs, feed mills, cold chain infrastructure, Biofloc, Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS), cage culture and other modern fisheries interventions based on requirements of the State Government. Further, a state-of-art wholesale fish market has been constructed at Chandauli to boost fisheries in eastern region of Uttar Pradesh. Besides, a Pangasius cluster has also been identified in Sidharth Nagar district for the aquaculture development in fast track mode in eastern region of Uttar Pradesh.

 (d):     The Government is promoting enhanced fish production and income generation of fishers through the various interventions under PMMSY, including aquaculture expansion, infrastructure development, modern technologies, post-harvest management, cold chain facilities, value addition and market linkages. These interventions have contributed significantly to the growth of the fisheries sector in the country, including in Uttar Pradesh. During the implementation period of PMMSY, the fisheries sector in the country has recorded substantial growth, including, increase of annual fish production from 141.64 lakh tonne in 2019-20 to 197.97 lakh tonne in 2024-25, increase in fisheries export from Rs.46,662.85 crore in 2019-20 to Rs.73,890 crore in 2025-26, enhanced per capita fish consumption from 5-6 kg to 12-13 kg and enhanced aquaculture productivity from 3 tonne/hectare to 4.7 tonne per hectare. These initiatives are expected to further strengthen fisheries development and improve the livelihoods and incomes of fishers and small farmers in the eastern region of Uttar Pradesh.

This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Traditional Fisheries
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi

ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR-CMFRI) has assessed that the trawl-based landings have shown no palpable decline in fish landings during 2021-2025. As per the Marine Fish Stock Status of India (2022) publication of the ICAR-CMFRI, the marine fish stocks of the Indian waters are in good health, and 91.1% of the 135 fish stocks evaluated in different regions of the Indian EEZ were found sustainable. 

  1. ‘Fisheries’ is a state subject, and each Coastal State has its Marine Fishing Regulation Act (MFRA) for governance of fishing activities within the territorial waters up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline, including zoning of fishing areas for traditional and mechanised fishing vessels, mesh‑size and gear regulations, seasonal fishing bans, minimum legal-size limits for fish capture, prohibition of destructive fishing practices such as paired/bull trawling and use of artificial/LED lights, and prevention of juvenile fishing. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), under which activities such as installation of Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) in trawl nets for protecting the sea turtles, sea ranching, and installation of artificial reefs in coastal waters towards enhancing fish stocks are undertaken for safeguarding the livelihood interests of traditional fishers. PMMSY also promotes acquisition of deep-sea fishing vessels, open-sea cage culture, and mariculture, including seaweed farming to divert fishing pressure away from the inshore coastal waters.
  1. The ICAR-CMFRI has informed that it conducts long-term monitoring of marine fisheries and ecosystems using a statistically validated, FAO-recommended stratified multistage random sampling design. The ICAR-CMFRI generates high-quality time-series data on fish landings and fishing effort from over 1,300 landing centres along India's 11,000 km coastline to assess fish stock status and infer ecosystem changes. Further, Institute also informed that it implements national programmes on marine biodiversity, benthic ecosystem health, trophic interactions, and the impacts of bottom trawling.

This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
FISH PRODUCTION
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi

 The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India with effect from the Financial Year 2020-21 is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in the country. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India during the last six years has approved fisheries development projects of 34 States/Union Territories and other implementing agencies amounting to Rs.21,461 crore with Central share of Rs.9,571 crore and a sum of Rs.6,206 crore has been released to various States/UTs and other implementing agencies under PMMSY. State-wise details of the projects approved, central share and funds released during the last six years are furnished at Annexure-I.

The PMMSY during last five years of its implementation has made vital contribution towards augmentation of fish production, enhancement of fisheries exports and creating of livelihood and employment opportunities. The fish production in the country has increased from 141.64 lakh tonne (2019-20) to an all time record of 197.75 lakh tonne (2024-25), creation of direct and indirect employment opportunities to 58 lakh persons in fisheries and aquaculture related activities, increase of fisheries export from Rs.46,663 crore (2019-20) to Rs.73,890 crore (2025-26). The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog, Government of India has evaluated the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana along with other Centrally Sponsored Schemes and the evaluation study while underlining the impact created by PMMSY in the fisheries sector has recommended its continuation. The PMMSY has been continued till September, 2026 in its existing form. During the current financial year (2026-27), a Central budget of Rs.2500 crore has been allocated for this scheme.

The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) implemented by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India inter-alia provides financial assistance for setting up of Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) to economically empower the fishers, fish farmers and enhance their bargaining power. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India during the last five years (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26) has approved projects worth of Rs.544.86 crore for formation of 2195 FFPOs in the country with support in the form of incubation cost, management cost and equity grant.

This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
TRADITIONAL FISHERMEN AND FISH FARMERS IN TAMIL NADU
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi

 The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) is implementing various schemes and programs for holistic development of fisheries sector and to enhance the livelihood, income and socio-economic welfare of traditional fishermen and fish farmers in the country including Tamil Nadu, such as Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) (2020-21 to 2024-25), Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (2018-19 to 2025-26), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah Yojana (2023-24 to 2026-27) and Extension of the facility of the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) to the fishers and fish farmers to meet their working capital requirements. In the state of Tamil Nadu, a project titled "Establishment of Multipurpose Seaweed Park" has been sanctioned under the PMMSY at a total cost of Rs. 127.71 crore, including component of seaweed multiplication in Hub-I Centre at Valamavur in Ramanathapuram District.

Under PMMSY and schemes of State Government of Tamil Nadu implemented in Ramanathapuram district in the last three financial years (2023-2026), financial assistance in the form of subsidies, insurance coverage and livelihood support has been provided to traditional fishermen and fish farmers for various activities, as detailed in Annexure I.

 (c):      The details of fisheries infrastructure developed in Ramanathapuram district, including fishing harbours, fish landing centres, cold storage facilities, ice plants, fish processing units and aquaculture infrastructure are provided at Annexure II.

(d):    The Government organizes various skill development and capacity-building programmes for fishermen and fish farmers to enhance their technical skills, disseminate recent innovations and best practices in the fisheries sector, and promote sustainable livelihood opportunities. These training programmes contribute to the livelihood development and socio-economic upliftment of fisher families. 88 training programs covering about 5599 trainees were conducted in the previous 3 years for fishers and fish farmers in Ramanathapuram district. The details are given in Annexure III.

(e): The Government is implementing various schemes to promote sustainable fisheries and enhance the livelihood of traditional fishing communities in Ramanathapuram district. Financial assistance and institutional credit is provided for acquisition of 45 deep-sea tuna fishing vessels. In Ramanthapuram District 13,949 Fishermen and farmers are facilitated with access to institutional credit of Rs. 236.26 crore through the Kisan Credit Card (KCC). Further, mariculture activities such as seaweed cultivation and cage culture are being actively promoted to provide alternative livelihood opportunities for fishers and coastal communities. So far, 19,575 seaweed culture rafts and monolines and 499 cage culture units have been established in different districts of Tamil Nadu including Ramanthapuram under various Government schemes. In addition, skill development and capacity-building programmes are regularly organized on seaweed farming, aquaculture and mariculture practices, value addition of fishery products, dry fish processing, preparation of ready-to-eat fish products, boat driving, marine engine repair and maintenance, net crafting, and recycling of waste fishing nets to enhance the technical skills and income-generating capacity of beneficiaries.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
PMMSY IN KERALA
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi

 The Department of Fisheries, Government of India through its schemes, policies and programs has been taking up several initiatives towards holistic development of fisheries sector in all the States and Union Territories (UTs) including in Kerala. During last 5 years and current financial year under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) fisheries developmental projects amounting to Rs.1413.91 crore has been approved to the Government of Kerala. Under the PMMSY, the district wise allocation and beneficiary selection are done by the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. The Government of Kerala has informed that out of the total projects approved to Kerala under PMMSY, projects amounting to Rs. 8.85 crore has been allocated to the Ernakulam Parliamentary Constituency, and out of this Rs. 8.62 crore has already been released. The year-wise details of the funds allocated and released towards Ernakulam Parliamentary Constituency as reported by Government of Kerala is annexed.       

The Government of Kerala has also informed that the activities have been approved under PMMSY in Ernakulam inter-alia include Biofloc culture, Re-Circulatory Aquaculture System (RAS), brackishwater farming, cage culture, ornamental fisheries, fish marketing kiosks and  Matsya Seva Kendras. It is also informed that the approved projects are in various stages of implementation.

(c) There is no proposal pertaining to Ernakulum constituency is pending in the Department of Fisheries, Government of India.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
TRADITIONAL FISHERFOLK IN KERALA
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi

 The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) is implementing various schemes for holistic development of fisheries sector in all States/UTs including Kerala. The major schemes include Blue Revolution Scheme (2015-16 to 2019-20), extending Kisan Credit Card (KCC) to fisheries (since 2018-19), Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) (2018-19 to 2025-26), ‘Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana’ (PMMSY)’ (2020-21 to 2026-27), and a new Central Sector Sub-scheme viz. Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) (2023-24 to 2026-27). Enhancing fish production, ensuring sustainability of resources, strengthening of value chain, employment generation, safety & security of fishers and socio-economic wellbeing of fishers and fish farmers have been the core of these initiatives.

During last five years and current financial year (FY 2026-27) under PMMSY, DoF, GoI has accorded approvals to the fisheries development proposal of Government of Kerala amounting to Rs. 1413.91 crore. The approved activities inter-alia include livelihood support to fishers during fishing ban period, support to traditional fishers for procurement of boats and nets, establishment of integrated modern coastal fishing villages, establishment of climate resilient coastal fishing villages, additional and alternate livelihood activities such as bivalve cultivation, cage culture, ornamental fisheries, fish markets & kiosks, cold chain facilities, live fish vending centres, need based training and skill development programmes and development of fishing harbours and marketing facilities etc.

 The Central Government allocates Superior Kerosene Oil (SKO) on a quarterly basis, but its distribution within a State/UT under the Public Distribution System (PDS) is entirely managed by the respective State/UT Government. The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoP&NG) being the nodal Ministry on the subject matter has informed that as kerosene is a polluting fuel and adversely impacts public health, the PDS Kerosene allocation to States/UTs including Kerala have been rationalized since 2010-11. Till date, 21 States/UTs have become PDS Kerosene free. Government has formulated a new “PDS Kerosene Allocation Policy” for the period of 2025-26 to 2027-28 after stakeholders consultation including the Government of Kerala. As per the said Policy, the allocation is made to States/UTs under single category “PDS SKO” on quarterly basis for cooking & lighting and for special needs. Further, the State Governments have been given the liberty to sub-allocate PDS SKO for cooking and lighting or for special needs (fisheries, mela, exhibitions, pandemic, calamity etc.) based on their specific requirement. Distribution of PDS SKO within State/UT under PDS network is carried out by concerned State/UT. Scale and Criteria of distribution is, accordingly, also decided by respective State/UT.

MoPNG has further informed that under the new policy, the Government of Kerala has been allocated 22,704 KL PDS SKO for the year 2025-26 as against total allocation of 4,368 KL PDS SKO for the year 2024-25 which reflects an increase of 419.78 %. During the FY 2025-26 out of the allocated quantity of 22,704 KL the State uplifted 17,724 KL with a lapse of 4,980 KL.

It is also informed that, in view of the prevailing geo-political situation an adhoc allocation of 1716 KL PDS SKO was also made for cooking and lighting to the State vide MoPNG’s letter dated 12.03.2026 for upliftment till 30th June 2026. Out of the allocated quantity, the state uplifted 1512 KL only lapsing 204 KL. Further, an allocation of 4068 KL/quarter has been made to the State of Kerala for Q1 (April-June, 2026) and Q2 (July-September, 2026), 2026-27.

This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
BLUE ECONOMY PROJECTS IN ANDHRA PRADESH
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi

 The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) has been implementing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY):  A scheme to bring about Blue Revolution through sustainable and responsible development of fisheries sector in India’ in all States and Union Territories (UTs) including the State of Andhra Pradesh, since 2020-21. Under PMMSY, for the development of fisheries and fisheries infrastructure in the State, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has approved proposals of the Government of Andhra Pradesh at a total cost of Rs 2328.89 crore, with a central share of Rs 681.38 crore. An amount of Rs 445.05 Crore has been released to the State based on the State's utilization. The year-wise details of projects approved, fund sanctioned and released during the last six years under PMMSY for furnished at Annexure I.

 The major fisheries infrastructure projects approved under PMMSY for development of fisheries in the State of Andhra Pradesh include (i) establishment of 5 fish feed plants, (ii) 16 cold storages and ice plants, (iii) 6 modern fish landing centres, (iv) 3 modern fishing harbours, (v) modernization of fishing harbour at Vishakhapatnam and (vi) 1 integrated Aqua Park. In addition, 15 Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV) and one Fish Brood Bank have also been sanctioned.

 The Government is closely monitoring developments in the global trade environment, including geopolitical situations, through regular engagement with stakeholders and export promotion agencies. While no separate State-specific assessment has been carried out on the impact of the West Asia conflict on seafood exports from Andhra Pradesh, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has undertaken several initiatives to address emerging trade challenges. These initiatives include a Seafood Exporters Meet in April 2026, New Delhi and National Workshop on Seafood Exports at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh in June 2026, wherein issues relating to market diversification, Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), non-tariff barriers, traceability, logistics and export competitiveness were deliberated with stakeholders. Despite the prevailing global geopolitical and trade challenges, various efforts taken by the Government of India has resulted in India's seafood exports recording an all-time high of 19.72 lakh metric tonnes valued at ₹73,890.46 crore (US$ 8.46 billion) during the financial year 2025–26.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Flash Report on Central Sector Infrastructure Projects worth ₹150 crore and above
PAIMANA Portal tracks 1,847 Infrastructure Projects worth ₹40.54 lakh crore as of June 2026
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) continues to strengthen monitoring of Central Sector infrastructure projects through its PAIMANA platform, enabling improved tracking, timely reviews, and data-driven decision-making across Ministries. The portal tracks 1,847 Infrastructure Projects worth of ₹40.54 lakh crore as of June 2026.

Key Highlights

  • As of June 2026, 1,847 ongoing infrastructure projects, with a total revised cost of ₹40.54 lakh crore, are being monitored across 17 Central Ministries/Departments. The cumulative expenditure incurred on these projects stands at ₹21.97 lakh crore, accounting for approximately 54.18 per cent of the revised project cost, indicating steady progress in project implementation.
  • A significant proportion of projects are at advanced stages, with 709 projects (~39%) achieving over 80% physical progress, while 337 (~19%) have crossed 80% financial completion. The data also reflects a balanced pipeline, with projects distributed across early and advanced stages of implementation.
  • The Transport & Logistics sector (as per the DEA’s Harmonized Master List) accounts for the highest number of ongoing projects (1341 projects), with revised estimates of ₹22.32 lakh crore underscoring priority to connectivity-driven infrastructure growth.
  • 1,847 ongoing infrastructure projects include 769 Mega projects (project cost of ₹1,000 crore & above) with an original cost of ₹30.51 lakh crore, and 1,078 Major projects (project cost below ₹1,000 crore and up to ₹150 crore) amounting to ₹5.10 lakh crore.
  • Physical and financial progress broadly move in tandem, with a large number of projects clustered at the initial (0–20%) and advanced (81–100%) stages, indicating a pipeline of newly-started projects alongside many nearing completions. While physical progress exceeds financial progress in the 81–100% range, financial progress is relatively higher in the early stages, reflecting upfront expenditure patterns in project implementation.

 

Ministry/ Departments-wise progress of Infrastructure Projects

  • Ministry of Road Transport & Highways accounts for the highest number of projects, with 1022 projects (55%), and a share of total revised project cost of ₹9.89 lakh crore (24%), highlighting its central role in national infrastructure development.
  • Ministry of Railways is implementing 255 projects (14%), with a total revised project cost of ₹8.69 lakh crore (21%).
  • Ministry of Coal accounts for implementing 121 projects (7%), with a total revised project cost of ₹2.22 lakh crore (6%).
  • The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Ministry of Power, Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, and the Department of Water Resources, River Development & GR are implementing 105, 98, 50, and 40 projects, with associated revised costs of ₹4.33 lakh crore, ₹5.71 lakh crore, ₹3.65 lakh crore, and ₹2.04 lakh crore, respectively.
  • The remaining 156 projects (8%), with a total revised cost of ₹4.02 lakh crore (10%), are distributed across various Ministries/Departments including Higher Education, Civil Aviation, Steel, Telecommunications, Labour & Employment, Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Health & Family Welfare, Mines, DPIIT, and Sports. (Refer Annexure I)

Sector-wise (as per DEA’s Harmonized Master List of Infrastructure) Progress of Infrastructure Projects

  • Transport & Logistics remains the dominant sector, accounting for 55% of total revised project cost (₹22.32 lakh crore) across 1,341 projects (73% of the total Projects), underscoring the central role of Roads & Highways, Railways, Aviation, Urban Public Transport, Shipping, and Inland Waterways in economic integration and logistics efficiency.
  • The Energy sector follows with 26% of aggregated revised cost (₹10.38 lakh crore) across 207 projects, reflecting sustained emphasis on Oil & Gas infrastructure, electricity generation, transmission and distribution networks, and energy storage systems.
  • Communication infrastructure, with a project cost of ₹2.64 lakh crore (7%) across 15 projects, represents targeted interventions aimed at strengthening digital connectivity.
  • Water & Sanitation projects account for ₹2.08 lakh crore (5%) across 56 projects, highlighting continued focus on essential urban services.
  • Social & Commercial infrastructure, comprising 88 projects with a revised project cost of ₹0.94 lakh crore (2%), reflects selective investments in education, healthcare, real estate, and tourism, hospitality and wellness.
  • Projects classified under ‘Others’, amounting to ₹2.18 lakh crore (5%) across 140 projects, indicate diversification across sectors such as coal, steel, metals, and mining.

(Refer Annexure II)

 

Completed Projects and New Additions

  • During June 2026, notable commissioned projects include-
    • Project – “Rajasthan Refinery Project” (₹ 79,459 crore) of Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas.
    • Project – “Transmission System for Kurnool Wind Energy Zone/ Solar Energy Zone Part-A and Part-B” (₹ 3,546.94 crore) of Ministry of Power.
    • Project - “6L of Varadharajula to Kumarajapet from km 0.000 to km 43.800 of NH-716B Pkg-I” (₹ 1,887.38 crore) and “Delhi-Amritsar-Katra Expressway Phase-I Pkg-IV from Junction with Jind-Karnalroad NH-709A near Alewa village to Junction with Ambala-Kaithal-Hissar road NH-152 near Kharak Pandwa village Km 91400 to Km 120250” (₹ 1,578.66 crore) of Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.
  • During June 2026, 17 additional projects were brought under the monitoring of PAIMANA. Of these 14 are from the Ministry of Road Transport & Highway and 3 are from Department of Telecommunications. These include:
  • “6 Lane Greenfield Varanasi- Ranchi- Kolkata Highway from Donoreshan village to junction with  NH-20 in Bongabar village from km 288.600 to km 325.500 Pkg -11” (₹ 1,856.12 crore)
  • “6L Greenfield Varanasi- Ranchi- Kolkata Highway from junction with  NH-20 in Bongabar village to junction with NH-30 in Lepo village from km 325.500 to km 358.500 Pkg -12” (₹ 1,525.52 crore)
  •  “Development of 6-lane Greenfield Southern Ludhiana Bypass from intersection with NH-44 near Village Rajgarh to intersection with Delhi Katra Expressway NE-5 near Village Ballowal, km 0000 to km 25240” (₹ 1,424.55 crore).

Next date of Press Release: Flash Report for the month of July 2026 would be released on 25th August 2026.

Note

  1. PAIMANA is a centralized web-based portal for monitoring of Central Sector Infrastructure Projects costing ₹150 crore & above.
  2. The press release summarizes highlights from the MoSPI’s Flash Report (June 2026) on Central Sector Infrastructure Projects (₹150 crore and above), available at https://paimana-proj.mospi.gov.in/ or via the QR code.

 

  1. Nearly 70% of data are updated via API’s on PAIMANA-CRIP portal  that serves as a national central repository of infrastructure  projects contributing towards standardized infrastructure monitoring and support informed decision-making for nation-building.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
India's Index of industrial production records growth of 7.3% in June 2026
Quick Estimates of Index of Industrial Production and Use- Based Index for the Month of June 2026 (Base 2022-23=100)
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi

In June 2026, Index of Industrial Production recorded a 7.3% year-on-year growth, supported by 7.8% growth in Manufacturing sector and strong growth of 10.6% in Electricity & Gas Supply sector.

The Quick Estimate of Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is released on 28th of every month (or next working day if 28th is a holiday). The index is compiled with data received from source agencies, which in turn receive the data from the producing factories/ establishments. These Quick Estimates will undergo revision in subsequent releases as per the revision policy of IIP.

2.  Key Highlights:

  1. The IIP growth rate for the month of June 2026 is 7.3 percent which was 5.1 percent (Quick Estimate) in the month of May 2026.
  2.  The growth rates of the sectors, Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of June 2026 are 1.0 percent, 7.8 percent, 10.6 percent and 6.1 percent respectively.
  3. The Quick Estimate of IIP stands at 123.1 against 114.7 in June 2025. The indices of Industrial Production for Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of June 2026 stand at 110.0, 123.3, 131.0 and 145.7 respectively.
  4. Within the Manufacturing sector, 19 out of 23 industry groups at NIC 2 digit-level have recorded a positive growth in June 2026 over June 2025. The top three positive contributors for the month of June 2026 are – “Manufacture of electrical equipment” (34.0%), “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers” (17.5%), and “Manufacture of food products” (10.8%).
  5. In the industry group “Manufacture of electrical equipment” item groups “Electrical Apparatus for Switching or Protecting Electrical Circuits (e.g., Switchgear, Circuit Breakers/Switches, Control/Meter Panels) and Parts Thereof”, “UPS and Solid-State Drives”, and “End-Face Connectors for Optical Fibres and Cables” have shown significant contribution in growth.
  6. In the industry group “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers”, item groups “Auto Components, Spares and Accessories”, “Passenger Cars”, and “Commercial Vehicles” have shown significant contribution in growth.
  7. In the industry group “Manufacture of food products”, item groups “Tea”, “Rice (Other Than Basmati)”, and “Starch, All Types” have shown significant contribution in growth.
  8. As per the Use-Based Classification, the indices stand at 119.5 for Primary Goods, 140.5 for Capital Goods, 124.2 for Intermediate Goods and 132.9 for Infrastructure/ Construction Goods for the month of June 2026. Further, the indices for Consumer durables and Consumer non-durables stand at 119.8 and 115.4 respectively.
  9. The corresponding growth rates of IIP as per Use-Based Classification in June 2026 over June 2025 are 4.9 percent in Primary Goods, 14.2 percent in Capital Goods, 9.3 percent in Intermediate Goods, 7.5 percent in Infrastructure/ Construction Goods, 7.7 percent in Consumer durables and 4.9 percent in Consumer non-durables (Statement III).  Based on Use-Based Classification, top three positive contributors to the growth of IIP for the month of June 2026 are Intermediate Goods, Primary goods, and Capital Goods.
  1. Along with the Quick Estimate of IIP for the month of June 2026, the indices for May 2026 have undergone final revision in the light of the updated data received from the source agencies.
  2. The Quick Estimates for June 2026 and the final revision for May 2026 have been compiled at weighted response rates of 86.7 percent and 93.1 percent respectively.
  3. Details of Quick Estimates of the Index of Industrial Production for the month of June 2026 at Sector, Sub-Sector, 2-digit level of National Industrial Classification (NIC-2025), by Use-Based Classification and are given at Statements I, II (A, B, C, D) and III respectively. Also, for users to appreciate the changes in the industrial sector, Statement IV provides month-wise indices for the last 13 months, by industry groups (as per 2-digit level of NIC-2025), sectors and Sub-Sectors.
  4. Release of the IIP for July 2026 will be on Friday, 28th August 2026.

Note: -

  1. This Press Release (English and Hindi Version) is also available at the Ministry’s Website -http://www.mospi.gov.in.
  2. Detailed data pertaining to IIP is available at  https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/macroindicators?product=iip

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
DEVELOPMENT OF RESERVOIRS AND AMRIT SAROVARS
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi

 (a): The Government of India in the Union Budget, 2026-27 has announced the development of fisheries and aquaculture by undertaking integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in the country including Bastar  constituency in Chhattisgarh. The initiative reinforces the Government’s objective to harvest the untapped fisheries potential from reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, strengthening livelihoods of fishermen in the reservoirs and engagement of women self-help groups (SHGs), fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPO) for the development of fisheries in Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. The key components of this initiative  includes strengthening quality seed production by establishing hatchery, promotion of cage and pen culture in reservoir, providing boats and nets to reservoir fishermen, promotion of composite fish culture and integrated fish farming in the Amrit Sarovar, establishment of fisheries infrastructure such as fish feed mill, cold storage, ice plant, fish kiosk and retail fish market, fish transport vehicle and fish value addition units.

(b) to (d): The selection of the Reservoirs and Amrit sarovars  by the  Department of Fisheries (DoF), Government of India (GoI) has been done in consultation with States and Union Territories (UTs), considering the perennial water availability and fisheries potential of the identified reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. Accordingly, 12 number of reservoirs and 5 numbers of Amrit Sarovars from Bihar and 27 reservoirs and 5 Amrit Sarovars from Chhattisgarh including Kosardeda reservoir from Bastar Constituency has been selected. District-wise reservoir selected in Chhattisgarh in consultation with the State Government is at Annexure-III. 

(e) The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) with the objective of enhancing fishers’ income in the country is promoting involvement of Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups and fisheries cooperatives under the Integrated development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. This includes the formation of Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups, and fisheries cooperatives, as well as support for existing ones, in the selected reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars.

(f) The investment for the implementation of the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars is to be based on the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the States and Union Territories (UTs). The  unit cost and funding pattern are as per the existing guidelines of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY).

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
GAIS FOR FISHERMEN
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Government of India is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with a total investment of Rs. 20,750/- crore from the financial year 2020-21 to till date for development of fisheries in all States/Union Territories.  The scheme inter-alia provides social security measure to fishers, fish workers through group accidental insurance coverage to both marine and inland fishers and allied fish workers wherein the entire insurance premium amount is shared between the Centre  and State in the ratio of 60:40, 90:10 for the Himalayan & North Eastern States and in the case of the Union Territories, the entire premium amount is paid by the Centre. The insurance coverage provided under the PMMSY includes (i) Rs.5,00,000/- against death or permanent total disability, (ii) Rs.2,50,000/- for permanent partial disability and (iii) hospitalization expenses in the event of accident for a sum of Rs. 25,000/.  The year wise and State/UT wise details of claims filed, claims approved, claims rejected, claims pending, and total compensation disbursed under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) for fishermen since 2020 21 are furnished at Annexure-I.

(b)       During the last five years (2021-22 to 2025-26) and current finance year (2026-27) of the implementation of the PMMSY, an average of 35.74 lakh active fishers have been enrolled under the Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS), annually. The average State/UT-wise details of fishers enrolled and coverage percentage of the total estimated fishermen population under Group Accident Insurance Scheme (GAIS) are furnished at Annexure-II.

(c):       Besides, under the erstwhile Blue Revolution scheme, insurance coverage for fishers was modest, with relatively lower benefit amounts. Based on the suggestions received from State Governments and evaluation of Blue Revolution Scheme, the GAIS coverage under PMMSY has been significantly enhanced both in scale and value to provide increased financial security and risk mitigation to fishers. As such, the sum assured has been increased from ₹2 lakh to ₹5 lakh for accidental death or permanent total disability, ₹1 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh for permanent partial disability, along with ₹10,000/- to Rs. 25,000 hospitalization support, compared to much lower limits under the erstwhile Blue Revolution scheme.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
ALLOCATION OF FUNDS FOR TAMIL NADU UNDER PMMSY
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:54PM by PIB Delhi

 (a): The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI) accorded administrative approvals for the implementation of projects under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) in Tamil Nadu during the period 2020-21 to 2025-26 with a total approved outlay of Rs.1,240.5778 crore. This comprised a Central share of Rs.480.0906 crore, State share of Rs.455.6139 crore, and beneficiary contribution of Rs.272.8488 crore covering both Beneficiary and Non-Beneficiary components. The approved project outlay represents the total financial allocation for the entire scheme period, whereas the Central share is released in phases by the DoF, GoI based on the progress of implementation, submission of Utilisation Certificates (UCs), and compliance with scheme guidelines, etc. Accordingly, the Central assistance is released from time to time, and it does not represent a deficit in the approved project outlay.

(b): The details of central funds released under PMMSY to Tamil Nadu, year wise during the last three years (2023-24 to 2025-26) and the details of central funds released under PMMSY in Tirunelveli District of Tamil Nadu are provided at Annexure. The subsidy amounts are directly transferred to the beneficiaries bank accounts through Electronic Clearing Service (ECS).

(c): To promote Deep Sea fishing in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), the DoF, GoI had introduced a sub-component namely “Assistance for Deep Sea Fishing” and another component of “Conversion of Trawlers into Resource Specific Deep-Sea Fishing Vessels” under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) on Blue Revolution implemented from 2015-2020. These sub-components were introduced to provide financial assistance to traditional fishermen for promotion of deep-sea fishing in the coastal States/UTs including Tamil Nadu. The financial assistance to traditional fishermen for acquisition of Deep Sea Fishing Vessels (DSFVs) has also been continued under the PMMSY at the rate of 40% subsidy for General Category and 60% subsidy for SC/ST/Women beneficiaries. Support for DSFVs is also provided by the DoF, GoI, under the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF). Under PMMSY, financial support is provided to traditional fishers for acquisition of deep-sea fishing vessels (DSFVs) as well as for Upgradation of Existing Fishing Vessels for Export Competency. Under the schemes of Blue Revolution, PMMSY, and the FIDF, projects amounting to Rs.1,314.81 crore have been sanctioned for the acquisition of 1,205 deep-sea fishing vessels by traditional fishers including the fishers of the Tamil Nadu State. The development and modernisation of infrastructure has been accorded high priority under the schemes implemented by the DoF, GoI. Infrastructure projects worth Rs 187.9 crores were sanctioned under Blue Revolution Scheme in Tamil Nadu, which includes fishing harbour project at Mookaiyur and fish landing centre at Kunthukal. Projects worth Rs 155.57 crores have been sanctioned under the PMMSY in Tamil Nadu, which includes three fishing harbour projects viz. modernization of Chennai fishing harbour, upgradation of Pazhayar fishing harbour, maintenance dredging of Colachel fishing harbour; and four fish landing centre projects viz. Nettukupam fish landing centre, Thazankuppam fish landing centre, Arangankuppam fish landing centre, and Goonankuppam fish landing centre. Under Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) scheme, 16 Nos of Fishing Harbours and 57 Fish landing centre have been sanctioned in Tamil Nadu at total project cost of Rs.1988.35 crore.

(d): The subsidy/concession rate on fuel to the fishermen has been provided by the respective State Governments/Union Territories, by exercising their powers to frame their own taxation and welfare policies for the fisheries sector. It is informed by the State Government of Tamil Nadu that the Government is providing sales tax exempted diesel to the fishermen for reducing the operational cost of their fishing boats (Both mechanized fishing boats and motorized country crafts) and also providing subsidized industrial kerosene to the motorized country crafts operated in the districts of Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari districts.

Under these scheme, Government of Tamil Nadu is providing sales tax exempted diesel of  19,000 L / year / craft to 4,500 Mechanised fishing boats, sales tax exempted diesel of  4,400 L / year / craft to 13,500 Motorized country crafts and subsidized industrial kerosene of 3,700 L / year / craft to around 7500 Motorized country crafts. 

This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Makes Rooftop Solar Accessible for All with Subsidy Support and Low-Interest Financing
Posted On: 28 JUL 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi

In order to ensure the affordability of rooftop solar (RTS) systems for middle-income and economically weaker households under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY), following provisions have been made:

  1. Higher central financial assistance for the first two kWp of RTS capacity.
  2. Availability of collateral-free loan from nationalized banks at a concessional interest rate of repo-rate plus 50 bps, i.e., 5.75% per annum for the present, with a tenure of 10 years.
  3. Included RESCO/Utility-Led Aggregation (ULA) Models.

The year-wise budgetary allocation and funds released under the PMSG: MBY is given below: -

As a result of various the measures taken to accelerate the deployment of RTS systems under the scheme, a total of 39,72,447 RTS system has been installed covering 48,02,717 households as on 22.7.2026.

While the electricity bills of consumers installed RTS under the scheme have been largely reduced, over 18.93 households reported even zero electricity bills for some months, depending on their self-consumption of electricity.
