item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM’s address in the 136th Episode of Mann Ki Baat on 26.07.2026
Posted On: 26 JUL 2026 12:08PM by PIB Delhi

My dear countrymen, Namaskar.

There are certain days in our lives that do not require a calendar to be remembered. Today, the 26th of July, is one such date. Today is ‘Kargil Vijay Diwas’. This day fills us with pride. This day reminds us of the extraordinary courage of our brave soldiers. Towering peaks of Kargil, harsh weather, the challenge posed by the enemy—our soldiers faced every such circumstance, yet their spirit was greater than every challenge. They sacrificed their all for the defence of Maa Bharati. Today, on ‘Kargil Vijay Diwas’, I respectfully bow to all the brave martyrs and soldiers.

Friends,

The India of today not only remembers her heroes but also conveys their saga to the new generation. With this very sentiment, a special ‘Shaurya Vijay Yatra’ has been organized this year. Having started on the 14th of July from the National War Memorial in Delhi, this motorcycle rally will reach the Kargil War Memorial in Dras.

Its message is - "One Ride, One Nation, One Salute." This journey reminds us that the sacrifice made for the nation can never be forgotten.

Friends,

Today, alongside the courage of her soldiers, India is also continuously strengthening her technological capabilities. A few days ago, INS Mahendragiri was inducted into the Indian Navy. This modern warship has been designed and built in India itself. More than 75 percent of the materials used in it are indigenous. It is a symbol of the growing strength of an ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’. This very month, the DRDO also successfully tested the Pinaka Long-Range Guided Rocket. Behind this success lies the collective perseverance of our scientists and engineers. Only two-three days ago, the DRDO also successfully tested the Kusha missile.

Friends,

Whether it is defence production, defence exports, or political cooperation with friendly nations—India is continuously scaling new heights. Earlier this month, I was in Indonesia, where a major agreement regarding BrahMos and Astra missiles was concluded. Global confidence in India’s defence equipment and technology is growing.

This ‘Kargil Vijay Diwas’, let us pay tribute to our immortal martyrs and further strengthen our resolve to build a secure, capable, and self-reliant India.

My dear countrymen,

In the previous episode of ‘Mann Ki Baat’, I spoke to you about the ‘Catch The Rain’ campaign. I had appealed that this campaign to conserve every drop of rain be turned into a mass movement. The message of ‘Catch The Rain’ is very simple: conserve the water right where and when the rain falls. That is why a special nationwide campaign has been underway since the 4th of July. Under this initiative, fresh momentum is being given to rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, the rejuvenation of old water bodies, and tree plantation. I am delighted to see overwhelming participation from people everywhere - be it villages or cities, panchayats or social organizations.

At some places, silt is being removed from old ponds, while at others, wells and stepwells are being revived. Borewells no longer in use are now serving as channels for groundwater recharge.

Friends,

Around 1,500 ponds have been constructed in the Sidhi district of Madhya Pradesh. 'Amrit Sarovars' have been restored in Narsinghpur. Significant water storage capacity has been developed in Nashik, Maharashtra. In Nandyal, Andhra Pradesh, all gram panchayats have joined this campaign, and old ponds have been made functional again. Our cities as well are not lagging behind either; encouraging results from this campaign are visible in Korba (Chhattisgarh), Bhubaneswar (Odisha), and Vizianagaram (Andhra Pradesh). Come, let us also take responsibility for a pond, well, or stepwell in our vicinity - save every drop of water. Every drop saved today serves as the greatest asset for the future of coming generations. My dear fellow citizens, the Commonwealth Games began in Glasgow, just a few days ago. Every Indian is constantly extending one’s best wishes to the Indian contingent. It is their wish that all players and athletes perform exceptionally well and win the hearts of the people.

Friends,

Our youth have achieved remarkable feats in sports recently. PV Sindhu has become the first Indian to win the Japan Open title in badminton; the entire nation is proud of this achievement of hers. The Indian women's cricket team also won its first-ever Test match at the Lords Stadium in London. This is a historic victory; our team won the match by a massive margin of 270 runs. But that is not all - in the long history of Lord’s, this was the first Test match played by a women's team. It was on this very ground that India won her first Cricket World Cup in 1983. Now, our 'Nari Shakti' has brought glory to the nation there.

Friends,

There are also small initiatives that hold great significance. I learned about one such sports-related initiative in South Chittoor, Ernakulam, Keralam. A school there has a Sanskrit club where a teacher, Abhilash ji, is popularizing Sanskrit in a unique way. This project has been named 'Aksharakanduk'; it explains Sanskrit letters in a simple manner by linking them to terms used in football. This makes learning enjoyable while also fostering a deeper connection between people and sports.

My dear countrymen,

Every Indian is filled with pride following the successful launch of 'Vikram-1' last Sunday. All of us Indians were witness to this historic moment for India's Space sector. It is India's first rocket developed by the private sector. Our young innovators achieved something that was once difficult to even imagine… they displayed remarkable skill, passion, and patience. For a long time, our Space sector remained closed to the private sector, denying many interested young people the opportunity to showcase their talent. Keeping the interests of the youth in mind, we opened up the space sector to private enterprise, and today, the world is witnessing the results.

Friends,

Our young friends are also bringing glory to India in the field of science. Science Olympiads are among the most important competitions in the world. A large number of students participate in these events. Olympiads in Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and Mathematics were held just this month. The Indian contingent delivered a spectacular performance in these competitions. In the Physics Olympiad, all five of our students won gold medals, and India secured the top rank.

Over the past decade, students from our country have won either a gold or a silver medal in every Physics Olympiad. In the Chemistry Olympiad, too, all our students won gold medals. This has been our best performance so far. All our students also won medals in the Biology Olympiad, including a gold medal. On the other hand, in the Mathematics Olympiad, our students secured two gold and four silver medals. I am immensely proud of the nation's youth power. It is heartening to see the culture of Olympiads and Hackathons steadily growing in India. I am confident that more and more young people across the country will show interest at such forums and keep the flag of India flying high.

My dear countrymen,

When one possesses both talent and the passion to achieve something, every path becomes easy. A glimpse of that is evident in the efforts currently being made regarding Kashmir's traditional 'Vagu' mat. It is crafted out of reeds and paddy straw. The tradition of making this mat dates back many years. The process begins with harvesting grass and reeds from the marshy regions of Kashmir. After drying them in the sun and sorting the materials, the hand-weaving process begins.

It takes approximately four days for two artisans to complete a single mat. This mat is both unique and eco-friendly. A major feature is that it provides coolness in the summer and warmth in the winter. While it used to be found in every Kashmiri household, its usage had declined over the last few years. Amidst that, Ghulam Hussain ji from Srinagar and his daughter, Tanzila ji, took a pledge. Both dedicated themselves to reviving the tradition of the 'Vagu' craft. Ghulam Hussain ji comes from a very humble background. He faced numerous challenges in this endeavour. However, his resolve to preserve ‘Vagu’ remained unflinched. And within no time, many people began joining this initiative. Ghulam Hussain ji significantly advanced this craft. He also received local government support for his mission.

Today, ‘Vagu’ is rapidly gaining popularity and reaching other parts of the country. I am immensely proud of everyone associated with this effort. Today, we are all emphasizing local products; we are moving forward with the mantra of ‘Vocal for Local.’ In this context, do consider making Kashmir’s ‘Vagu’ a part of your home as well.

Friends,

In our country, tea is not merely a beverage—it embodies a sense of togetherness. Whether it is the start of the day, a meeting with friends, or spending quality time with family, tea becomes an integral part of every occasion. In fact you are, well aware of my own bond with tea.

However, the tea I am bringing into discussion today has not only offered taste but has also infused the lives of many women with the fresh aroma of self-reliance. Women associated with a Self-Help Group in Lakhiwala village, Bijnor district, Uttar Pradesh, have created ‘Vidur Prerna Swadeshi Herbal Tea.’ It contains natural ingredients such as lemongrass, Giloy, Mulethi (licorice), Tulsi, raw turmeric, cinnamon, cardamom, and fennel seeds. Due to its unique taste and qualities, this tea has quickly carved a niche for itself among the people. This herbal tea has garnered immense appreciation at the Mahakumbh in Prayagraj and the International Food Festival in Delhi; even visitors from abroad have shown interest in it.

Friends,

The most inspiring aspect is how it all began. This entire venture started with an investment of just one lakh rupees. Today, the brand has reached major institutions across the country. This initiative demonstrates that when local knowledge, nature, and the self-confidence of women come together, even a small effort can initiate significant change.

My dear countrymen,

People across the country are fulfilling their responsibility towards nature through the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign. When society connects with this sentiment, beautiful and inspiring examples emerge. Friends, the incredible power of public participation was witnessed in Ahmedabad. In the Bhadaj area, over 3.5 lakh saplings were planted within a single hour, with more than 25,000 people joining the effort. School children, NCC cadets, volunteers, and ordinary citizens—everyone participated in this campaign. In the coming years, these saplings will grow into a dense urban forest. This achievement has been recorded in the Guinness Book of World Records.

Friends,

The remarkable resolve of the people was also evident in Uttar Pradesh under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign, where over 35 crore saplings were planted in a single day - on the 12th of July. As a Member of Parliament representing a constituency in UP, this is a matter of special pride for me.

My dear countrymen,

Trees are not just for humans; they are also home to countless living creatures. After nearly 60 years, the Indian Grey Hornbill is once again making its abode in the Gir forests of Gujarat. This is the result of years of conservation and restoration efforts in Gir. The Hornbill is often referred to as the ‘farmer of the forest.’ They eat these fruits and disperse the seeds far and wide; from these very seeds, new trees grow in the forest. In this way, a single bird helps make the forest lush and green again. I would urge all of you to connect a special occasion in your lives with nature—plant a tree in your mother's name. A small sapling planted today can become a legacy of greenery, clean air, and a beautiful future for generations to come.

My dear countrymen,

We all know that plastic pollution poses a major challenge to the global environment today. Waste from single-use plastic continues to harm nature for years; therefore, proper disposal of plastic is crucial. Friends, a magnificent example of 'Waste to Wealth' has emerged from Sitamarhi in Bihar. Here, waste is being recycled to create attractive benches. About 40 kilograms of single-use plastic are consumed to make one bench. These benches are not only strong, durable, and comfortable but also eco-friendly. They are installed in government schools, parks, and public spaces.

This initiative is also raising awareness among people about environmental conservation. Both local bodies and the district administration play a vital role in this effort. That’s also generating local employment opportunities. This initiative in Sitamarhi shows us that 'Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle' is no longer just a slogan but is becoming a part of our lives.

Friends,

You might recall that in the last episode of 'Mann Ki Baat', I had spoken of 'Ganesh Utsav'. I had urged everyone to worship idols of Ganesha ji made from our country's own clay.

Instead of Ganesh ji made of POP or those imported from abroad, we should install Ganesh ji made from indigenous soil in our homes. Many people have sent me messages and shared their thoughts on this subject. People have told me that they have heeded my request. They have resolved to install idols of Ganesha ji made from local clay. People have written in to say that this topic was previously discussed in ‘Mann Ki Baat,’ and that it helped them take the right steps at the right time. I reiterate my appeal: this time, for Ganpati Puja, install an idol of Ganesha ji made from the soil of our own land in your home and worship it. This effort of yours will, in a way, be a form of worshipping nature itself.

My dear countrymen,

I will now tell you about a person who will make you feel very proud. He is someone actively working in the fields of science and innovation and gaining global recognition; yet, despite that, he remains deeply connected to his roots and never forgets to honour his homeland whenever the opportunity arises. That person is Dr. Ronaldo Laishram from Manipur. His name is Dr. Ronaldo, but professionally, he is an astrophysicist. He works in Japan and has been part of the team that discovered a massive cluster of young galaxies.

You might be wondering what exactly he has done. Well, he named this entire cluster the ‘Loktak Proto-cluster,’ linking it to a beautiful lake in Manipur. Loktak is a vast freshwater lake. ‘Phumdis’, the floating islands of vegetation in Loktak Lake create a unique landscape; it appears as if small islands are floating in a vast ocean. Similarly, these young galaxies in the universe form a massive structure. Today, Manipur’s Loktak is shining not only on the country's map but also across the vast cosmos. This achievement is a source of pride for every Indian. It teaches our young friends that they can scale new heights while remaining connected to their traditions. These are roots that can also light up the world of stars.

My dear countrymen,

In just a few days - on the 7th of August - our country will celebrate ‘National Handloom Day’. On this occasion, we celebrate the skills and creativity of our weaver brothers and sisters. These friends of ours are carrying forward traditions that have been passed down through generations.

Friends,

Every handloom garment tells the story of a specific region, a community, and the countless people associated with it. These are the people who are proudly dedicated to preserving India’s cultural heritage.

Today, I urge you to honour our weaver friends by encouraging handloom crafts. Come, let us further strengthen the spirit of being ‘Vocal for Local’.

Friends,

The way handloom is being promoted in the country today is improving the lives of a large number of people. We see many examples of this, from Pochampally to Patna and from Kuthampally to Kutch. Today, there are many individuals and groups infusing new energy and identity into our glorious handloom tradition. Some are carrying forward the beautiful tradition of ‘Pochampally Ikat’, while others are engaging women weavers to create wool products. Some are preserving Keralam’s traditional ‘Kasavu Kala’. This is also providing employment to our mothers and sisters.

Friends,

Another subject I would particularly like to mention is ‘Khadi’. We all know that ‘Khadi’ was very dear to Mahatma Gandhi. During recent years, ‘Khadi’ has become quite popular. Its sales have increased six-fold over the last 12 years. This sales figure has now reached nearly ₹8,000 crore. I urge all of you to definitely buy at least one product or the other made of Khadi, handloom, or handicraft during the upcoming festive season.

My dear countrymen,

If you were asked how many types of musical instruments exist in India, you would likely be left wondering! That is because we possess a vast array of musical instruments and the traditions associated with them. One such instrument is the ‘Chongpreng’ from Tripura; it is quite popular among the tribal communities there. Made of bamboo, this instrument features three strings. It produces a melodious tune that bears resemblance to the *Sarod*. For some reasons, its popularity among the youth had begun to wane. Amid that, Suraj Kumar Debbarma ji resolved to revive its popularity. Today, his efforts are bearing fruit; he performs using the Chongpreng as well as other traditional instruments from the region. He has a deep fondness for Kokborok folk songs, Baul songs & Bengali folk music. Now, I would like to play a short clip for you; it is a piece of music that you will never forget.

# Music #

Friends,

I am sure listening to that must have made you feel good. I am very proud of Debbarma ji; his efforts to popularize traditional music is truly commendable. I urge all of you to share information about traditional musical instruments found in your own vicinity on social media. Such efforts on your part will certainly connect others with traditional Indian music.

My dear countrymen,

Tomorrow, the 27th of July, marks the death anniversary of Bharat Ratna Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam ji. Dr. Kalam’s personality embodied many inspiring facets, yet the role of a teacher was closest to his heart. He inspired children and the youth to dream big. Coincidentally, this week we will also celebrate the pious festival of ‘Guru Purnima’. Our parents are our first teachers, while school teachers impart the knowledge of letters and learning. Guru Purnima is an occasion to express gratitude towards all such mentors. I offer my respectful Pranaam to all the teachers and mentors across the country. Friends, in just a few weeks, we will celebrate the grand festival of our Independence. 15th August is a day of pride for every Indian. It is a day to remember the countless heroes who dedicated their all for the freedom of ‘Bharat Mata’.

It is because of their sacrifice and devotion that we hold the Tricolour in our hands today; this Tricolour embodies the ideals of our Constitution.

Friends,

Over the past few years, the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign has united the entire nation with a remarkable spirit. The celebration of the Tricolour is visible in every home and every street. This year too, we must carry forward the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign with great enthusiasm. We must display the Tricolour at our homes with the utmost respect.

Friends,

Every year before 15th of August, you send me myriad ideas and suggestions. This year as well, please do share your thoughts on MyGov. I look forward to your suggestions.

Friends,

That’s all for today’s ‘Mann Ki Baat’. We will meet again next month with stories of many new achievements and inspiring efforts by our countrymen; until then, I take leave of you.

Thank you very much; Namaskar.

*****

MJPS/ST/VK

Prime Minister expresses gratitude to brave soldiers on Kargil Vijay Diwas
Posted On: 26 JUL 2026 9:48AM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today stated that on Kargil Vijay Diwas, our nation expresses gratitude to the brave soldiers for their extraordinary courage and commitment towards securing India.

The Prime Minister noted that their valour in the face of the most formidable conditions will forever remain a source of national pride. He observed that their unwavering patriotism and devotion to duty will continue to inspire generations.

In a post on X, the Prime Minister shared:

"On Kargil Vijay Diwas, our nation expresses gratitude to the brave soldiers for their extraordinary courage and commitment towards securing India. Their valour in the face of the most formidable conditions will forever remain a source of national pride. Their unwavering patriotism and devotion to duty will continue to inspire generations."

item.title: Rajasthan Chief Minister Shri Bhajanlal Sharma launches ‘Bharat Taxi’ service in Jaipur
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Cooperation
item.description: Ministry of Cooperation Rajasthan Chief Minister Shri Bhajanlal Sharma launches ‘Bharat Taxi’ service in Jaipur Realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Sahakar Se Samriddhi”, ‘Bharat Taxi’, under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, is bringing a new revolution to the transport sector through the cooperative model Cooperatives make the common citizen self-reliant and accord dignity to his labour — Shri Murlidhar Mohol Nearly 8 lakh registered Sarathis and 41 lakh customers join Bharat Taxi; around Rs 77 crore directly credited to…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Cooperation
Rajasthan Chief Minister Shri Bhajanlal Sharma launches ‘Bharat Taxi’ service in Jaipur
Realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Sahakar Se Samriddhi”, ‘Bharat Taxi’, under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, is bringing a new revolution to the transport sector through the cooperative model
Cooperatives make the common citizen self-reliant and accord dignity to his labour — Shri Murlidhar Mohol
Nearly 8 lakh registered Sarathis and 41 lakh customers join Bharat Taxi; around Rs 77 crore directly credited to Sarathis’ accounts so far — Shri Murlidhar Mohol
Rajasthan among the country’s leading States in grain storage, e-PACS and linkage with national cooperative societies — Shri Murlidhar Mohol
‘Bharat Taxi’ will provide Sarathis not only employment, but also ownership, dignity and participation in the institution’s profits — Shri Bhajanlal Sharma
Bharat Taxi is an initiative that will create new employment opportunities for Rajasthan’s youth and give fresh impetus to the State’s tourism and mobility sectors — Shri Bhajanlal Sharma
Memoranda of Understanding exchanged with Rajasthan Police, Saras, Jaipur Municipal Corporation and Jaipur Metro
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:42PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of “Sahakar Se Samriddhi” and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, an important initiative was undertaken today towards transforming the country’s mobility sector through cooperation, technology and inclusive development. Rajasthan Chief Minister Shri Bhajanlal Sharma launched the ‘Bharat Taxi’ service in Rajasthan at a programme held at the Harish Chandra Mathur Rajasthan State Institute of Public Administration in Jaipur. Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol, Rajasthan Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Gautam Kumar Dak, Member of Parliament from Jaipur Smt Manju Sharma, Chief Secretary of Rajasthan Shri V. Srinivas, Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India, Dr Ashish Kumar Bhutani, Principal Secretary, Cooperation Department, Rajasthan, Dr Samit Sharma, senior officials of the Government of Rajasthan, representatives of the cooperative sector and Sarathis associated with Bharat Taxi were present on the occasion.

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that Bharat Taxi is among the new initiatives of the Ministry of Cooperation that have broadened the scope and reach of cooperation during the past five years. He said that under the guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, cooperation is no longer confined only to Co-operative Credit Societies, but has expanded to sectors such as agriculture, dairy, fisheries, insurance, exports, storage, digital services and now transportation. Today, around 8.60 lakh cooperative societies are functioning in 30 different sectors across the country, with more than 32 crore members associated with them.

Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that Rajasthan has made a historic and distinctive contribution to the cooperative movement. One of the country’s earliest cooperative societies was established at Deeg in Bharatpur in 1904, while the establishment of the Rajasthan State Cooperative Bank in Jaipur in 1953 provided a strong foundation to the State’s cooperative sector. Today, around 42,000 cooperative societies are functioning in Rajasthan, with nearly 1 crore 35 lakh members. He said that the traditions of cooperation, collective action, water conservation and protection of nature have existed for centuries in Rajasthan’s rural culture, and cooperation is the modern economic expression of this very spirit.

The Union Minister of State for Cooperation said that after the establishment of an independent Ministry of Cooperation in 2021, more than 152 initiatives have been launched to strengthen the cooperative sector. Under the computerisation of PACS, around 80,000 PACS have been approved and nearly 63,000 PACS are operating on the digital system. Through Model Bye-Laws, PACS have been enabled to undertake more than 25 types of economic and business activities. The Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited, National Cooperative Organics Limited and National Cooperative Exports Limited have been established to provide farmers with quality seeds, markets for organic products and opportunities for the export of agricultural produce.

Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that Bharat Taxi is taking this broad cooperative transformation to taxi drivers in cities. In other private aggregator models, a driver is merely a service provider, whereas in Bharat Taxi, “the Sarathi is the owner”. A Sarathi is a member and shareholder of the cooperative institution, is entitled to representation on the Board of Directors and a share in the institution’s profits, and the amount for every trip is credited directly to his account. He said that nearly 8 lakh registered Sarathis and around 41 lakh registered customers have joined Bharat Taxi. Around 11,000 trips are being completed every day and nearly Rs 77 crore has so far been deposited in the accounts of Sarathis.

The Union Minister of State for Cooperation said that after Delhi and Gujarat, the launch of Bharat Taxi in Maharashtra and now Rajasthan marks an important phase in the national expansion of the cooperative-based mobility model. There are plans to extend this service to around 500 cities across the country in the coming period. He expressed confidence that Rajasthan would become a leading partner in this transformation and set a new example of a safe, reliable and Sarathi-centric transport system.

Referring to Rajasthan’s achievements in the cooperative sector, Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that the State is a leader in the implementation of the world’s largest grain storage scheme. Construction of 200 warehouses each approved during 2024-25 and 2025-26 has been completed. Around 5,650 PACS have been converted into e-PACS and more than 10 crore online transactions have been carried out through these PACS, accounting for nearly one-third of the country’s total transactions. Around 4,900 PACS in the State are engaged in three or more businesses, while nearly 6,750 PACS have become members of the Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited. He also appreciated the establishment of Sahakar Bhawan in Jaipur and the decision to provide 50 acres of land for BBSSL’s tissue culture laboratory.

On the occasion, Rajasthan Chief Minister Shri Bhajanlal Sharma said that Bharat Taxi is a transformative initiative that will advance the resolve of “Sahakar Se Samriddhi” in the State. He said that by creating employment and local economic opportunities through cooperation, dignified livelihoods can be made available to young people close to their villages, cities and families. The State Government has placed special emphasis on broadening the membership of cooperative institutions, and 10 lakh new members have been connected with cooperation during the past one year.

Shri Bhajanlal Sharma said that in Bharat Taxi, the Sarathi is not merely a driver, but a co-owner of the institution. Membership and shareholding give him a sense of ownership in his work, confidence and dignity. He said that when a person receives a stake in his work, his efficiency, hard work and motivation to progress increase manifold. A small enterprise or self-employment opportunity can become the first step towards major economic progress for a young person. The Rajasthan Chief Minister said that the Bharat Taxi model does not merely provide employment to the common citizen, but also offers ownership and dignity. A major share of the earnings will remain with the Sarathis and they will have a direct stake in the institution’s progress. He said that an accident insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh is also being provided under this initiative, ensuring respect for the labour of Sarathis, protection of their rights and security of their future. Bharat Taxi is not merely a digital platform, but a symbol of the self-respect and economic empowerment of Sarathis.

Shri Bhajanlal Sharma said that Rajasthan has vast potential for local employment through cooperation in several sectors, including agriculture, dairy, minerals, handicrafts and tourism. Establishing processing units for agricultural and dairy products in villages and local areas will provide employment to youth in their own regions and reduce migration. He said that work is being undertaken in the State to expand cooperative institutions at every Gram Panchayat level, enhance milk collection and processing capacity and promote value addition of local products.

The Chief Minister said that Rajasthan’s tourism potential offers special opportunities for Bharat Taxi. Bharat Taxi can play an important role in providing safe and reliable last-mile connectivity to passengers travelling to the expanded Jaipur Metro network, the State’s historic forts, palaces, lakes, wildlife sanctuaries, religious sites and desert tourism destinations. He said that Bharat Taxi would give new momentum to the State’s tourism sector and create new income opportunities for Sarathis.

Shri Bhajanlal Sharma said that more than 30,000 Sarathis and nearly 7 lakh customers have so far joined Bharat Taxi in Jaipur, and thousands of trips are being completed every day. He said that these figures reflect the public’s growing trust in the cooperative-based digital model. The objective of connecting the whole of Rajasthan with the Bharat Taxi network will give a new direction to the State’s mobility system and play an important role in providing citizens with safe, reliable and transparent transport services.

The Chief Minister called upon the Sarathis to maintain the reliability of the service, courteous behaviour towards passengers and high standards of safety. He said that Bharat Taxi has the potential to become not only India’s, but the world’s most successful cooperative-based mobility platform, because the Sarathis themselves are its owners and the returns on their labour go directly to them instead of to any intermediary. He expressed confidence that Rajasthan would become a leading partner in this transformation and present a new example of cooperative-based modern transportation before the country.

During the programme, share certificates were presented to the best-performing Sarathis. Memoranda of Understanding were also exchanged with Rajasthan Police, Saras, Jaipur Municipal Corporation and Jaipur Metro for the expansion of ‘Bharat Taxi’ and its coordination with various public services. At the conclusion of the programme, Chief Minister Shri Bhajanlal Sharma flagged off the Bharat Taxi fleet comprising 60 cabs, 20 bikes and 20 autos. With the cooperation of the Government of Rajasthan, cooperative institutions, local bodies and public service organisations, the service will be expanded in a phased manner to different cities and tourism destinations across the State.

***

AK

(Release ID: 2289491)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Indian Defence Forces stand fully prepared to face any challenge, says Raksha Mantri on the eve of Kargil Vijay Diwas 2026
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:10PM by PIB Delhi

“Even as the enemy’s intentions remain unchanged and it continues to employ nefarious tactics such as proxy wars & infiltration, the Indian Defence Forces stand fully prepared to face any challenge,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh on July 25, 2026 during a commemorative event in Dras on the eve of the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas. Paying tribute to the bravehearts who secured India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War, Raksha Mantri said the courage, resolve and patriotism displayed under the harshest conditions continue to inspire both the military and the nation.

Expressing confidence in the defence forces, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that no one dares to cast an evil eye upon India as long as the patriotism and resolve of the valiant troops of the nation remain unwavering. Their courage enables every citizen to pursue and realise their dreams without fear, he added.

As Raksha Mantri interacted with the troops over Barakhana, he asserted that “While we feel a sense of pride recalling the Kargil victory, we must remember that the challenges facing us have not diminished”. He reiterated Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government’s commitment towards the welfare of soldiers, adding that sustained emphasis is being laid on defence modernisation to ensure that the military is equipped with world-class weaponry and training.

Shri Rajnath Singh acknowledged the defence forces for embracing the latest technologies, emphasising that their stories of valour and commitment are recognised not just nationally, but globally as well. “This century belongs to us; the future belongs to us. Given the strides we have made towards self-reliance, I am confident that our defence forces will become the best in the world in the times to come,” he said.

The event ‘Shaurya Bhoj’ at the Vishwanathan Stadium also featured a display of drones, robotic mules and Army Martial Arts Routine drills, as well as a cultural programme showcasing the rich heritage of the region. Raksha Mantri later joined the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh Shri Vinai Kumar Saxena, Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Northern Command Lieutenant General Pratik Sharma, other serving personnel, Kargil War veterans, gallantry awardees, Veer Naris, Next of Kin of the heroes, civil dignitaries and local citizens for the Shaurya Bhoj.

Shaurya Sandhya

Prior to ‘Shaurya Bhoj’, Shri Rajnath Singh graced ‘Shaurya Sandhya’ at the Kargil War Memorial, where patriotic tunes set the tone for a solemn tribute to the heroes of Operation Vijay. 10 Next of Kin of Kargil War heroes were felicitated in recognition of the courage, resilience and sacrifice of their families.

A Kalash containing ‘Veeron Ki Mitti’ was presented to Raksha Mantri. Inter-faith prayers offered by religious teachers were followed by the solemn Beating Retreat ceremony and the National Anthem. Thereafter, Raksha Mantri lit lamps at the memorial in homage to the soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during the war.

Yudh Sansmaran

The commemorative events began with ‘Yudh Sansmaran’ at Lamochen View Point, attended by Kargil War veterans, Next of Kin of the fallen soldiers and other dignitaries. The programme featured the screening of the Yudh Sansmaran film and a short video recounting the extraordinary acts of courage and valour of 40 heroes of Operation Vijay. The Next of Kin were felicitated, following which family members shared their cherished memories of the soldiers.

Gauravmay Sanskriti

The afternoon programme at Vishwanathan Stadium commenced with patriotic performances by the Ladakh Scouts Regimental Centre Band. It was followed by a spectacular motorcycle display by the ‘Shwet Ashwa’ team of the Corps of Military Police Centre and School, demonstrating precision riding, discipline and professional excellence.

Students presented a vibrant National Integration Dance, besides glimpses of Indian Army's growing integration of cutting-edge technologies for operations in high-altitude and challenging terrain. The programme was followed by ‘Vijay Bhoj’, bringing together dignitaries, veterans, serving personnel and the families of the heroes in a spirit of remembrance, gratitude and solidarity.

The celebrations will culminate on July 26, 2026, with Raksha Mantri paying homage to the heroes of ‘Operation Vijay’ on behalf of the nation during the 'Shradhanjali Samaroh'. The commemorations pay tribute to the 545 bravehearts who laid down their lives during the Kargil War - 537 personnel of the Indian Army, 05 of the Indian Air Force, 01 of the Border Security Force & 02 civilians - whose supreme sacrifice ensured India's victory and safeguarded the nation's territorial integrity.

****

VK/Nishant/Savvy

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Government Strengthens Nationwide Implementation of New Criminal Laws Through Training, Technology and Judicial Reforms
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi

As per information provided by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) came into force throughout the country with effect from 1 July 2024.

The States and Union Territories have taken necessary measures for their implementation, including issuance of relevant notifications and rules, adoption of digital applications and capacity building of stakeholders.

Training of police personnel and other State-level stakeholders is primarily undertaken by the respective State and Union Territory Governments. In addition, the Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D) has conducted capacity-building programmes and webinars for Master Trainers and other stakeholders across all 36 States and Union Territories.

Since 2024, BPR&D has trained 83,740 officers and stakeholders from the five pillars of the criminal justice system, including Master Trainers. The cadre/position-wise, State/UT-wise and year-wise details are given in Annexure-I. The Master Trainers have also been utilised by State training institutions for conducting further training programmes within the respective States and Union Territories. The details of such training are given in Annexure-II.

As per the latest ‘Crime in India’ report released in 2024, the State/UT wise cases registered for organised crimes and terrorism are given in Annexure-III.
The data related to the number of cases registered wherein the provision of electronic evidence and community service, were availed is not maintained  by the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The Nyaya Sanhitas has been implemented throughout the country with effect from 01 July 2024, including the State of Madhya Pradesh. Further, ‘Police’, and ‘Public Order’ are State-list subjects as per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. The responsibilities to maintain law and order, protection of life and property of the citizens including investigation and prosecution of crime and criminals rest with the respective State/UT Governments and are competent to deal with such offenses under the extant provisions of law, which also includes the implementation of the Nyaya Sanhita. However, the Central Government supplements their efforts by providing financial support for augmentation of criminal justice infrastructure under various schemes, including the Inter-Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) 2.0, Schemes for Modernisation of Forensic Capacities and Nirbhaya Fund-supported projects.

As per information provided by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh, several steps have been taken for effective implementation of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 throughout the State, including Satna District. Judicial Officers have been imparted orientation and training through the Madhya Pradesh State Judicial Academy. Necessary amendments have been carried out in the Case Information System (CIS) and e-Courts software to facilitate implementation of the new criminal laws. The District Judiciary is regularly monitored through the administrative side of the High Court to ensure smooth transition and expeditious disposal of cases. The future roadmap includes continuous capacity building of Judicial Officers and court staff, strengthening digital court infrastructure, effective implementation of e-Courts Phase-III, greater use of technology for case management, and improving accessibility, transparency and efficiency to provide citizen-centric criminal justice delivery.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Eight Constitution Amendments Enacted in the Last Twelve Years, Government Informs Parliament
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Constitution of India was amended eight times during the last twelve years and the details of the said Constitution Amendment Bills, as enacted, are as under:

  1.  

The Constitution (Ninety-Ninth Amendment) Act, 2014 (relating to the National Judicial Appointments Commission to replace the collegium system for appointing judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts)
  1.  

The Constitution (One Hundredth Amendment) Act, 2015 (relating to the land boundary agreement between India and Bangladesh)
  1.  

The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016 (relating to the Goods and Services Tax in India)
  1.  

The Constitution (One Hundred and Second Amendment) Act, 2018 (relating to constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes)
  1.  

The Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019 (relating to reservation for Economically Weaker Sections in Government jobs and educational institutions)
  1.  

The Constitution (One Hundred and Fourth Amendment) Act, 2019 (relating to extending the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the

 

Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for another ten years, until January 25, 2030)
  1.  

The Constitution (One Hundred and Fifth Amendment) Act, 2021 (relating to amendments in article 342A and consequential amendments thereto in articles 338B and 366 of the Constitution)
  1.  

The Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 (relating to reservation of seats for women in the House of People and in the Legislative Assemblies of the States)

 

This information was given by the Union Minister of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Ji, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

***

Samrat/PN/Sagar

item.title: ECI's Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls Being Conducted in Phases with Multiple Safeguards to Protect Eligible Voters
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Law and Justice
item.description: Ministry of Law and Justice ECI's Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls Being Conducted in Phases with Multiple Safeguards to Protect Eligible Voters Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi As per the Press Note of the ECI, the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is being carried out in several phases across the country, with the objective of ensuring that the electoral rolls are accurate, up-to-date, and free of ineligible or duplicate entries, while ensuring that no eligible elector is left out. Phase I: The SIR was first undertaken in the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
ECI's Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls Being Conducted in Phases with Multiple Safeguards to Protect Eligible Voters
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi

 As per the Press Note of the ECI, the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is being carried out in several phases across the country, with the objective of ensuring that the electoral rolls are accurate, up-to-date, and free of ineligible or duplicate entries, while ensuring that no eligible elector is left out.

Phase I: The SIR was first undertaken in the State of Bihar, ahead of the Elections to the State Legislative Assembly in the year 2025. The exercise involved house-to-house enumeration by Booth Level Officers (BLOs), distribution and collection of enumeration forms, publication of a draft electoral roll and providing a specific period for filing claims and objections, and subsequent publication of the final electoral roll after due verification.

Phase II: The similar process was followed during Phase-II for nine States and three Union territories, namely, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep and Puducherry from October, 2025 to April, 2026.

Phase III: The SIR is presently underway or proposed in the remaining States/UTs not covered in Phase I and II, including the National Capital Territory of Delhi, in accordance with a schedule notified by the ECI, which is subject to revision from time to time based on operational requirements.

Throughout the exercise, consolidated data on enumeration, additions, deletions, and corrections is compiled and published by the ECI on its official website and by the respective Chief Electoral Officers of the States/UTs concerned, as the revision progresses.

As per the Press note of the ECI, the deletions during SIR are carried out only after due verification by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) through house-to-house enumeration, and broadly fall under the following categories: (i) death of the elector; (ii) permanent shifting of residence; (iii) duplicate entries of the same elector in more than one place; and (iv) electors found untraceable despite repeated visits.

The following safeguards have been put in place by ECI to prevent wrongful deletion of eligible electors:

(i) Prior intimation and door-to-door visits by BLOs, with a minimum of two-three attempts before an elector is treated as untraceable;

(ii) Deletion only after recording reasons in the prescribed enumeration format and following the process under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960;

(iii) Publication of draft electoral rolls and a statutory period for filing claims and objections (Forms 6, 7 and 8) before the roll is finalised;

(iv) Provision for appeal before the District Magistrate/designated appellate authority and further recourse to the Chief Electoral Officer;

(v) Deployment of Booth Level Agents (BLAs) nominated by political parties to verify entries and flag discrepancies during the enumeration and claims/objections stages.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in its judgment dated 27.05.2026 in W.P. (C) 640 of 2025 titled Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. vs. Election Commission of India & Ors., examined the legality of the SIR process and held, inter alia, that the SIR exercise is within the statutory mandate of ECI under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and is consonance with the Election Commission's constitutional obligation under Article 324 to ensure free and fair elections.

Further, it is evident from the Press Note of the ECI, that it carries out internal quality checks at each stage of SIR, including cross-verification of BLO enumeration through supervisory officers, random sample audits of deleted entries, and public disclosure of draft and final rolls to enable scrutiny by political parties and electors. Grievances received during the claims and objections period are examined and, where found valid, names are restored before finalisation of the roll.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Ji, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

***

Samrat/PN/Sagar

(Release ID: 2289473)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Government Strengthens Accessible Legal Services and Inclusive Digital Justice for Persons with Disabilities
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has undertaken several measures to make available affordable, quality and speedy legal services to the common man, including persons with disabilities. The legal Services Authorities (LSA) Act, 1987 provides for free and competent legal services to the weaker sections of the society including Persons with Disabilities. As per Section 12(d) of the LSA Act, 1987, “a person with disability as defined in clause (i) of section 2 of the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1955” is entitled to free legal aid.

NALSA is also implementing a specific Scheme for Persons with Disabilities named NALSA (Legal Services to Persons with Mental Illness and Persons with Intellectual Disabilities) Scheme, 2024. This Scheme aims to ensure that legal services are responsive to the specific legal and social needs of persons with mental illness and persons with intellectual disabilities. Under this Scheme, specialised ‘Legal Services Unit for Persons with Mental Illness & Persons with Intellectual Disabilities (LSUM) called ‘Manonyay’’ units have been established in all States/UTs except Lakshadweep.  The LSUM is the primary institutional mechanism for the delivery of legal services to persons with mental illness and persons with intellectual disabilities at Mental Health Establishments, Police Stations, Courts, Railway Stations, Bus Stands, Beggar’s Homes, Women’s Protection Homes, Child Care Institutions, Prisons, Detention Centres, Front Offices and through Home Visits.

The details of the persons with disabilities provided legal services under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 during the last three financial years is as under:

 

Financial Year

Number of persons with disabilities provided legal services

2023-24

11,591

2024-25

8,313

2025-26

15,280

 

The Government is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for development of infrastructure facilities for the District and Subordinate Courts by augmenting the resources of the State Governments/UTs for construction of Court Halls, Residential Units for Judicial Officers, Lawyers’ Hall, Digital Computer Rooms and Toilet Complexes. As per guidelines of the Scheme, the States/UTs ensures that the proposed infrastructure have disabled-friendly design. The building design are in conformity with the requisite norms/accessibility standards as laid down by Central Public Works Department, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, from time to time.

The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with the objective of strengthening the use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system. The eCommittee, Supreme Court of India is the governing body that oversees the eCourts project and provides policy planning, strategic direction and guidance to the project for effective implementation of all components.

Under eCourts Project Phase III, there are 24 components that have several significant measures devised to foster the creation of a robust and accessible digital infrastructure for citizens including persons with disabilities. Provision has been made for providing enhanced accessible ICT enabled facilities to persons with disabilities, at a budgetary outlay of Rs. 27.54 crore and using S3WaaS platform (Secure, Scalable and Sugamya Website as a Service) that makes the website friendly for persons with disabilities, at a budgetary outlay of Rs. 6.35 crore. S3WaaS platform has features for easy visibility of content for partially and completely visually challenged citizens.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Ji, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

***

Samrat/PN/Sagar

(Release ID: 2289470)

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
eCourts Phase III Progress Monitored Regularly; e-Filing 3.0 Implemented Across All District Courts in Punjab
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:02PM by PIB Delhi

The eCourts Mission Mode Project Phase-III is being implemented through an institutional framework wherein the e-Committee, Supreme Court of India provides policy inputs and the High Courts are implementing agencies. The implementation of the Project, including in the State of Punjab, is monitored on a regular basis through periodic review meetings, progress reports and continuous coordination with the concerned High Court to facilitate timely implementation of the approved components under the Project.

The status of digital court infrastructure, district-wise are at Annexure-I.

E-filing 3.0 has been implemented in all the District Courts in the State of Punjab. Adequate digital facilities and infrastructure for virtual hearings have been provided in the District Courts in the State of Punjab as per the guidelines of the eCommittee, Supreme Court of India.

Annexure-I

STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF LOK SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 978 FOR 24.07.2026 REGARDING E-COURTS PHASE-III PROJECT IN PUNJAB

The status of digital court infrastructure, district-wise:

item.title: Centre Continues Support for Judicial Infrastructure Development in Andhra Pradesh Under Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Law and Justice
item.description: Ministry of Law and Justice Centre Continues Support for Judicial Infrastructure Development in Andhra Pradesh Under Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:01PM by PIB Delhi The primary responsibility for development of infrastructure facilities for District and Subordinate Courts rests with the State Governments/UTs. However, to augment the resources of States/UTs, Central Government has been implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for the Development of Infrastructure Facilities for Judiciary in the District and Subordinate Courts since…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Centre Continues Support for Judicial Infrastructure Development in Andhra Pradesh Under Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:01PM by PIB Delhi

The primary responsibility for development of infrastructure facilities for District and Subordinate Courts rests with the State Governments/UTs. However, to augment the resources of States/UTs, Central Government has been implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for the Development of Infrastructure Facilities for Judiciary in the District and Subordinate Courts since 1993-94. The Scheme covers five components namely Court Halls, Residential Units for Judicial Officers, Lawyers’ Halls, Toilet Complexes and Digital Computer Rooms. The Scheme is appraised by a third party agency across the country including the State of Andhra Pradesh for its effectiveness. The Scheme is also appraised by the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee (DRPSC).

Under the CSS, projects are identified by the States/UTs and High Courts concerned. After receipt of the detailed demands from the States/UTs, tentative allocation of funds to States/UTs is done and Mother Sanction is issued to States/UTs. The States/UTs can incur expenditure on the identified projects within the limit of Mother Sanction while adhering to the guidelines of CSS. For Financial Year 2026-27, Mother Sanction of Rs 8.79 crore has been issued to the State of Andhra Pradesh. The Scheme had sunset date of 31.03.2026 and has been temporary extended up to 30.09.2026.

As per information provided by the State Government of Andhra Pradesh, the district-wise details of court infrastructure presently functional and under construction across Andhra Pradesh, including Nellore District are at Annexure-I.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Government Says Future Tribunal Law Will Align with Supreme Court Judgments on Appointments and Judicial Independence
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 9:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its judgment dated 19.11.2025 in the matter of Madras Bar Association vs. UOI, W.P.(C) No.1018 of 2021, inter-alia, vide para-142 of the said judgement, has struck down certain provisions of the Tribunal Reforms Act, 2021.

The various judgments of the Supreme Court including the above judgment apply to the appointments, tenure and service conditions of the members and Chairpersons of the tribunals.

Further, the statutory provisions as and when enacted, would inter-alia also holistically take into consideration the various judgments of the Hon’ble Supreme Court and the directions on the subject including the judicial independence of the tribunals.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Ji, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Law and Justice
item.description: Ministry of Law and Justice High Court Judges' Transfers and Appointments Governed by Constitutional Provisions and Memorandum of Procedure. Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 8:59PM by PIB Delhi Article 222 of the Constitution of India stipulates that the President may, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, transfer a Judge from one High Court to any other High Court. As per the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) for appointment and transfer of High Court Judges, the proposal for transfer of High Court Judges is initiated by the Chief Justice of India in consultation…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
High Court Judges' Transfers and Appointments Governed by Constitutional Provisions and Memorandum of Procedure.
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 8:59PM by PIB Delhi

Article 222 of the Constitution of India stipulates that the President may, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, transfer a Judge from one High Court to any other High Court. As per the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) for appointment and transfer of High Court Judges, the proposal for transfer of High Court Judges is initiated by the Chief Justice of India in consultation with four senior-most puisne Judges of the Supreme Court.

The MoP further provides that the Chief Justice of India is also expected to take into account the views of the Chief Justice of High Court from which the Judge is to be transferred, as also the Chief Justice of the High Court to which the transfer is to be effected, besides taking into account the views of one or more Supreme Court Judges who are in position to offer views. The personal factors relating to the concerned Judge, including the Chief Justice, and his response to the proposal, including his preference of places, should invariably be taken into account by the Chief Justice of India and the first four puisne Judges of the Supreme Court before arriving at conclusion on the proposal. All transfers are to be made in public interest i.e. for promoting better administration of justice throughout the country. No timeline has been prescribed in the MoP for transfer of judges from one High Court to another.

Appointment of Judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts is made under Articles 124, 217 and 224 of the Constitution of India and according to the procedure laid down in the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) prepared in 1998 pursuant to the Supreme Court Judgment of October 6, 1993 (Second Judges case) read with their Advisory Opinion of October 28, 2 1998 (Third Judges case). As per the MoP, the responsibility for initiation of proposals for appointment of Judges in the Supreme Court vests with the Chief Justice of India, while the responsibility for initiation of proposals for appointment of Judges in the High Courts vests with the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court, in consultation with two senior-most puisne Judges of the High Court. As per the MoP, the High Courts are required to make recommendations at least 06 months before the occurrence of a vacancy. For appointments to the High Courts, the views of concerned State Government are obtained in accordance with the MoP. The recommendations also have to be considered in the light of such other reports as may be available to the Government in respect of the names under consideration. The recommendations of the High Court Collegium, the State Governments and the Government of India are then forwarded to the Supreme Court Collegium (SCC) for advice.

 Appointment of Judges in the higher judiciary is a continuous, integrated and collaborative process between the executive and the judiciary. It requires consultation and approval from various Constitutional Authorities both at State and Central level. Only those persons whose names have been recommended by the SCC are appointed as Judges of the High Courts.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Ji, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
67 Fast Track Special Courts, Including 56 Exclusive POCSO Courts, Functional in Madhya Pradesh.
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 8:57PM by PIB Delhi

As per the information made available by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh, 67 Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including 56 exclusive POCSO Courts, are functional under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs). Of these, two FTSCs, including one exclusive POCSO Court, are functional in Ratlam district, while one FTSC is functional in Jhabua district, for the expeditious disposal of cases relating to rape and offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. No FTSC is functional in Alirajpur district.

The number of cases instituted, disposed of and pending before the FTSCs, including exclusive POCSO Courts, in Ratlam and Jhabua districts during the last two years is as under:

The establishment of District and Subordinate Courts, including Special Courts, falls within the administrative domain of the respective State Governments, in consultation with the High Courts concerned. Accordingly, the setting up of additional FTSCs is considered by the State Government in consultation with the concerned High Court, keeping in view the pendency of eligible cases and the availability of resources. At present, no proposal for setting up additional FTSCs is under consideration of the Government in the said Parliamentary Constituency.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Centre Allocates ₹2,010 Crore for Judicial Infrastructure and eCourts Modernisation in Union Budget 2026.
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi

Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for Development of Infrastructure Facilities for the District and Subordinate Courts, a sum of Rs. 810 crore has been allocated in the union budget 2026 for judicial infrastructure. In addition, sum of Rs. 1200 crore has been allocated in the union budget 2026 for the eCourts Project Phase-III being implemented for digitisation of courts including necessary training and capacity building programmes. Adequate budgetary provisions are made under these Schemes based on approved outlays and availability of funds. However, the expeditious disposal of cases depends on multiple factors including complexity of case, quality of investigation, availability of relevant evidence and presentation thereof by the Advocates, timely delivery of the court processes, active participation of the parties, judicial procedures etc.

The Government of India, in coordination with the State Government and the Judiciary, has taken several measures to ensure accessible, speedy and effective justice across the country, including in the Tonk–Sawai Madhopur Parliamentary Constituency. Financial assistance is provided under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for strengthening of court infrastructure. Tele-Law services are available through Common Service Centres (CSCs) to provide pre-litigation legal advice. Under the eCourts Project, digital services such as e-Filing, e-Pay, Virtual Courts, video conferencing and the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG) have been implemented. Free legal aid is extended through the Legal Services Authorities. Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms, including Lok Adalats and mediation, are also being promoted for expeditious resolution of disputes.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Ji, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Government Defers Proposal to Include Karnataka Reservation Act, 2022 in Ninth Schedule Pending Court Proceedings
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government had received a reference from the Government of Karnataka for inclusion of the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022 in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution. The Act, forming part of the State’s reservation framework, provides for 56 per cent reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes. The said Act, passed by the Karnataka State Legislature, has been challenged before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka and matter is sub-judice. In view of the same, it was decided that the request for the inclusion of the said Act in the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution may not presently be appropriate.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Ji, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
775 Fast Track Special Courts Functional Across 29 States/UTs; Centre Extends FTSC Scheme Till September 2026
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi

A Centrally Sponsored Scheme to set up Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), including exclusive POCSO (ePOCSO) courts was launched in October 2019, for the expeditious trial and disposal of pending cases related to rape and offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. The Scheme has been extended twice, with the last extension valid up to 31.03.2026 for establishment of 790 FTSCs. The Scheme has been temporarily extended upto 30th September, 2026.  As per the information made available by the High Courts, as of 30.04.2026, 775 FTSCs, including 398 exclusive POCSO (e-POCSO) Courts were functional in 29 States/UTs. The State/UT-wise details are given at Annexure-I.

The number of cases registered, disposed of and pending before Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) including exclusive POCSO courts, during the last three years, are as under:

The funds under the FTSC Scheme are released on the pattern of Centrally Sponsored Scheme (Central share: State share :: 60:40, 90:10) to cover the salaries of one Judicial Officer along with 7 support Staff per FTSC and a Flexi Grant for meeting the day-to-day expenses. The funds are reimbursed to the States/UTs after receipt of the expenditure statements from them. The Department has released a sum of ₹1259.51 crore to the States/UTs since its inception to ensure the smooth functioning of the courts. The State/UT-wise details of central share of funds released during the last three years including FY 2026-27 are given at Annexure-II.

To strengthen the functioning of FTSCs, regular review meetings are held via Video Conferencing with the States/UTs and the High Courts. The Hon’ble Minister of Law & Justice has written to Hon’ble Chief Ministers and Chief Justices of the High Courts regarding need for timely action and strict compliance with timelines under the POCSO Act and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. In addition, the performance of FTSCs is a regular agenda item in the Inter-State Zonal Council meetings to improve inter-governmental coordination and expedite justice delivery.

As regards the recruitment of judges and staff in courts, filling up of vacant positions of the judicial officers in District and Subordinate courts including the FTSCs, is the responsibility of the State/UT Governments and the concerned High Courts. As per the Constitutional framework, in exercise of powers conferred under proviso to Article 309 read with Articles 233 and 234 of the Constitution, the State/UT Government in consultation with the respective High Court frames the rules regarding the recruitment and appointment of Judicial Officers.

The primary responsibility for the development of infrastructure facilities for District and Subordinate Courts in the States/UTs, rests with the State/UT Governments. However, to augment the resources of the State /UT Governments, the Union Government has been implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the Development of Infrastructure Facilities for District and Subordinate Courts by providing financial assistance to the State/UT Governments in the prescribed fund sharing between Center and States since 1993-94. At present, there are five components of the Scheme for which Central assistance is granted to the States/UTs viz (i) Court Halls (ii) Residential Units (iii) Lawyers’ Halls (iv) Toilet Complexes and (v) Digital Computer Rooms. An amount of ₹4,519.47 crore has been provided as financial assistance to the States/UTs under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the Development of Infrastructure Facilities for Judiciary during the XV Finance Commission cycle.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Government Accelerates Digital Transformation of Judiciary Under eCourts Phase III to Reduce Case Pendency
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 8:51PM by PIB Delhi

Disposal of cases pending in various courts lies within the domain of the judiciary. However, the Government is fully committed to speedy disposal of cases and reducing pendency. The Government has taken several initiatives to provide an ecosystem for faster disposal of cases by the judiciary which, inter-alia, includes amalgamation of latest technologies under the e-Courts Mission Mode Project, better infrastructure for courts, policy and legislative measures in the areas prone to excessive litigation.

The Phase-III of the eCourts Project (2023-2027) was approved on 13.09.2023 with an outlay of Rs.7,210 crore. Phase III envisions a transition towards digital, paperless courts through large-scale digitisation of records, wider use of virtual hearings, interoperability across institutions and adoption of emerging technologies including Artificial Intelligence (AI), analytics and Optical Character Recognition (OCR). The current status of progress made under eCourts Phase-III is as under:

  1. 2977 court complexes are equipped with bandwidth speed ranging from 10 Mbps to 100 Mbps.
  2. 1.21 cr. cases have been filed through the e-filing platform.
  • iii. The e-payments system has processed transactions for court-fee worth Rs. 1,594 crore and fine worth Rs. 97 crore.
  • iv. Case Information System (CIS) 4.0 has been implemented in all courts, with enhanced privacy safeguards and integration with national platforms such as NJDG, e-filing, virtual courts and Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS).
  1. More than 35.57 lakh FIRs and 38.36 lakh Chargesheet have been received by the courts (CIS 4.0) digitally from CCTNS.
  • vi. The eSummons system has been introduced for electronic delivery of summons through email.
  1. Through the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG), litigants can access case information in respect of over 32.46 crore cases and over 39.79 crore orders/judgments.
  2. The courts have conducted over 4.15 cr. hearings through video conferencing, facilitating remote hearings of undertrials, witnesses and lawyers.
  • ix. Over 734 crore pages of court records including legacy records have been digitized across courts.
  1. To safely and permanently store court records, a robust digital vault “Judicial Digital Trustworthy Repository” has been developed.
  • xi. The JustIS app (22,534 downloads) helps the judges to effectively organise and monitor judicial work.
  1. 31 Virtual Courts have been established to enable online adjudication of traffic challans.
  2. 2,515 e-Sewa Kendras are functional across High Courts and District Courts to provide citizen centric services to lawyers and litigants.
  3. An AI based software tool called Legal Research Analysis Assistant [LegRAA] has been developed to aid judges in legal research and document analysis.
  4. The S3WaaS platform hosts 730 Courts websites, ensuring secure and accessible web infrastructure.

 

The details of funds released to various High Courts, as recommended by e-Committee, Supreme Court of India, under the eCourts Project during the last three years, are at Annexure.

In addition, several steps taken by the Government to reduce judicial delays and improve access to justice through technology and judicial reforms are as under:

  1. Under the Centrally Sponsored Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) Scheme, for the expeditious disposal of pending cases of Rape and POCSO Act, 775 Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs) including 398 exclusive POCSO (ePOCSO) Courts are functional across 29 States/UTs and have collectively disposed of 3,87,481 cases.
  2. Arrears Committees have been set up in all 25 High Courts and the District Courts to clear cases pending for more than five years.
  3. The Government has also enacted New Criminal Laws 2023, The Negotiable Instruments (Amendment) Act, 2018, The Commercial Courts (Amendment) Act, 2018, The Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018 with a view to reduce pendency.
  4. Alternate Dispute Resolution methods have also been promoted by the Government.
  5. Lok Adalat is an important Alternative Disputes Resolution Mechanism available to common people, where the disputes/ cases pending in the court of law or at pre-litigation stage are settled/compromised amicably.

****

Ministry of Law and Justice
Centre Strengthens Judicial Infrastructure in Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh Under Centrally Sponsored Court Infrastructure Scheme
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 8:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government has been implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for the Development of Infrastructure Facilities for the District and Subordinate Courts since 1993-94. The Scheme covers five components, namely Court Halls, Residential Units for Judicial Officers, Lawyers’ Halls, Toilet Complexes and Digital Computer Rooms. As per information provided by the High Courts of Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh, the details of available Court Halls and Residential Units for Judicial Officers in the district and subordinate courts in these States vis-à-vis the sanctioned strength of judges as on 31.05.2026 is as under:

Under the CSS, projects are identified by the States/UTs and High Courts concerned. After receipt of the eligible proposals from the States/UTs, tentative allocation of funds to States/UTs is done and Mother Sanction is issued to States/UTs. The States/UTs can incur expenditure on the identified projects within the limit of Mother Sanction while adhering to the guidelines of CSS. For Financial Year 2026-27, Mother Sanctions of Rs 5.33 crore and 5.195 crore have been issued to the State of Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh respectively.

In respect of the digital infrastructure for courts, comprehensive digital ecosystem has been created under the eCourts Mission Mode Project to support the entire lifecycle of a case from filing to final adjudication. For digitalization of courts, funds amounting to Rs. 151.73 cr. and Rs. 20.66 cr. have been released to the High Court of Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh respectively Under the Phase III of the eCourts Project.

This information was given by the Union Minister of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Ji, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

Samrat/PN/Sagar

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Government Strengthens Digital Justice and Legal Aid Infrastructure Across Odisha Under eCourts and Tele-Law Initiatives
Posted On: 25 JUL 2026 8:49PM by PIB Delhi

The details of Budget Estimates, Revised Estimates and actual expenditure during the last three years under the e-Courts Mission Mode Project, Tele-Law Programme, National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and Gram Nyayalaya Scheme, across the country including the state of Odisha are at Annexure I.

The State/UT-wise details of funds sanctioned, released and utilized under e-Courts Mission Mode Project Phase III, NALSA and Gram Nyayalaya is at Annexure II.

As per the information provided by the eCommittee, Supreme Court of India, in the State of Odisha, 16 ADR Centres have been constructed and are functioning in 16 districts including the districts of Ganjam and Kandhamal. For the remaining 14 districts including the districts of Boudh and Nayagarh, Mediation Centres are functioning in the office of the District Legal Services Authority.

For online adjudication of traffic challans, 31 virtual courts (asynchronous courts) have been set up across the country, including 1 in Odisha.

The status of courts under the e-Courts project, Tele-Law, legal aid clinics, and Gram Nyayalayas, district-wise, in Odisha including the districts of Kandhamal, Boudh, Nayagarh and Ganjam is at Annexure III.

Adequate budgetary provisions are made for additional judicial infrastructure, virtual courts, digital literacy programmes and legal aid facilities across the country including in all tribal and aspirational districts in Odisha, based on approved outlay and availability of funds. Financial assistance is provided under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for strengthening court infrastructure. Tele-Law services are available through Common Service Centres (CSCs) to provide pre-litigation legal advice. Under the eCourts Project, digital services such as e-Filing, e-Pay, Virtual Courts, video conferencing and the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG) have been implemented. Free legal aid is extended through the Legal Services Authorities. Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms, including Lok Adalats and mediation, are also being promoted for expeditious resolution of disputes.
